items.title: Praise won’t pay teachers’ bills — Atiku tells FG
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Atiku Abubakar, has told the Federal Government that praise will not ease the hardship facing Nigerian teachers, urging it to tackle the rising cost of food, transport, rent and electricity. Atiku said teachers were being asked to keep educating the nation’s children while their salaries struggled to keep pace with the cost of living, leaving some unable to afford basic needs for themselves and their families. He made the submission in a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, to mark World Teachers’ Day on Monday. Recalling his early education in Jada, Atiku said he still remembered the teachers who recognised his potential when few others did. “Of course, I appreciate Nigerian teachers. I am a product of their work and the education I received in their classrooms. I still remember the names and faces of my early teachers in Jada, who saw potential in a young orphan when few others did. They taught me arithmetic and grammar, but they also gave me a future,” he said. He said the depth of the hardship confronting teachers could be seen in the sacrifices some were now making simply to get to school and put food on their families’ tables. “When I hear of a teacher forced to walk miles because transport fares consume so much of their salary, or borrowing food on credit to feed their family before going to teach our children, my heart breaks. No nation can rise above the level of its teachers,” Atiku said. He said government recognition of teachers must go beyond annual speeches and messages, insisting that their welfare should be reflected in the conditions under which they live and work. “Government cannot praise teachers on this day and leave them to face hardship for the rest of the year. A commemorative message cannot pay a teacher’s bills. Respect must be reflected in fair conditions, reliable support and policies that make life affordable,” he said. Atiku also criticised President Bola Tinubu over his alleged inability to name a teacher or classmate from his school days, linking the issue to what he described as a failure to appreciate the struggles of educators. “It is both revealing and deeply embarrassing that Bola Tinubu cannot name a single teacher who stood before him or a classmate who sat beside him. Teachers are the architects of every nation’s future,” he said. “If he cannot honour the people who helped shape him, how can he understand the sacrifices teachers make today? Such a president cannot make life dignified or affordable for teachers—not in the country he leads, nor in the community he calls home.” Atiku further said his experience had given him an appreciation of the demands of teaching and the role educators play in building confidence, knowledge and opportunity. He said Nigeria could not secure its future while neglecting those responsible for educating its children, promising to pursue policies aimed at reducing the cost of living, supporting decent jobs and improving the welfare of families. “My promise is clear: I will work to make life affordable again. Teachers and families should not have to watch their incomes disappear on food, transport, rent and electricity. We will pursue policies that bring down the cost of living, support decent jobs and ensure that hard work can provide a dignified life,” Atiku said. The former vice president also apologised to teachers and Nigerians on behalf of what he described as a leadership that had failed to make their welfare a priority. “I apologise to Nigeria’s teachers and to all Nigerians on behalf of a leadership that has failed to make their welfare a priority. Teachers deserve more than praise, and Nigerians deserve a government that puts their lives and livelihoods first,” he said. Atiku thanked teachers across the country for their service, urging the country to match its appreciation of their contribution with meaningful support. The post Praise won’t pay teachers’ bills — Atiku tells FG appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: L’ Alliance islamique organise un atelier destiné à renforcer le rôle des enseignants dans la lutte contre l’extrémisme
items.description: La Coalition militaire islamique contre le terrorisme a organisé ce lundi à Nouakchott un atelier de formation intitulé « Formation des universitaires et des enseignants à la protection des jeunes contre l'idéologie extrémiste », dans le cadre de son programme destiné aux pays du Sahel. Cet atelier vise à renforcer les connaissances et les compétences des enseignants et des universitaires en matière de détection et de gestion des dérives idéologiques, à travers trois axes principaux : la notion de dérives idéologiques et son lien avec le crime terroriste, les facteurs qui y conduisent, ainsi que les méthodes utilisées par les groupes terroristes et extrémistes pour diffuser leur propagande auprès des jeunes et des adolescents. L’atelier aborde également le rôle de l’enseignant dans la détection des signes de dérive idéologique au sein du milieu éducatif, ainsi que les moyens d’y faire face afin de contribuer à la protection des jeunes et à leur sensibilisation. Le colonel ingénieur Al-Hassan Abdi Fleïvil, directeur de la documentation et de la sécurité militaire au ministère de la Défense, des Retraités et des Enfants des martyrs, a dit que cette formation visait à doter les participants des connaissances et des outils nécessaires pour comprendre le phénomène de l’extrémisme, ses discours et ses méthodes d’influence, ainsi qu’à renforcer leur capacité à y faire face dans les milieux éducatifs et universitaires avec efficacité et lucidité. Il a salué les efforts de la Coalition militaire islamique contre le terrorisme pour soutenir les États membres et renforcer leurs capacités dans le domaine de la lutte contre le terrorisme, notamment en ce qui concerne l’aspect idéologique et le renforcement des capacités, et a exprimé sa gratitude pour la participation des ministères des Affaires islamiques et de l’enseignement originel, de l’Éducation et de la Réforme du système éducatif, ainsi que celui de l’Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique, par le biais d’une sélection d’universitaires et d’enseignants. Pour sa part, le Dr Yahya bin Mohammed Abu Maghaid, chef du département des programmes préventifs dans le domaine idéologique au sein de la Coalition militaire islamique contre le terrorisme, a précisé que cet atelier s’inscrit dans une série d’activités menées par la Coalition dans le cadre du programme des pays du Sahel, qui s’étend sur cinq ans. Il a souligné que le choix du secteur de l'éducation s'explique par son rôle central dans la construction des sociétés, le développement de leurs connaissances et de leur prise de conscience, ainsi que dans le renforcement de leur capacité à faire face aux différentes menaces, au premier rang desquelles figure le terrorisme.

items.title: Oyebanji rewards Ekiti teachers with N70.5m
items.description: 203 public secondary schools now have ICT labs By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, on Monday rewarded outstanding teachers across the state with N70.5 million as part of activities marking the 2026 World Teachers’ Day. The beneficiaries, drawn from public primary and secondary schools, private schools and administrative cadres, were recognised for outstanding performance and commitment to duty. Speaking at the celebration in Ado-Ekiti, themed “Standing with Teachers: 60 Years of Protecting the Profession, Advancing its Status and Shaping Our Futures,” Oyebanji called for sustained investment in teachers’ welfare and modern learning facilities. The governor assured teachers of his administration’s continued commitment to their welfare and provision of conducive working environments, promising that outstanding emoluments, particularly leave bonuses, would be paid soon. Responding to a request by the teachers, Oyebanji disclosed that the state government would construct a new ultra-modern state library, which he said had been captured in the 2027 budget. “I have listened to the leadership of NUT and let me disclose that we will be constructing a befitting state library next year. It has been captured in the 2027 budget,” he said. Oyebanji said teachers remained central to the development of the nation’s human capital, stressing that their contribution to shaping future generations could not be quantified. He described the 2026 celebration as significant because it marked 60 years since the 1966 ILO/UNESCO Recommendation concerning the Status of Teachers, adopted in Paris. “This year’s celebration is historic. It marks the sixty years since the 1966 ILO/UNESCO recommendation concerning the status of teachers in Paris, establishing international standards concerning teachers’ rights and responsibilities,” he said. The governor said the theme also resonated with his administration’s education agenda and commitment to strengthening teachers’ professional identity. He disclosed that all 203 public secondary schools in the state now had ICT laboratories, while 125 had been equipped with 5KVA inverters and internet facilities. According to him, old school buildings had been renovated or rehabilitated across the schools, while perimeter fencing had been provided for 54 public secondary schools. He added that 48 public secondary schools had been equipped with CCTV cameras, with another 85 schools scheduled to receive the facilities within the month. Oyebanji also said his administration had continued to prioritise regular payment of salaries and the provision of revolving car and housing loans for eligible secondary school teachers. He said the government had also addressed personnel shortages through the recruitment of teachers into public primary and secondary schools. According to him, 5,530 teachers had been recruited in four years, comprising 430 teachers through the Teaching Service Commission in 2022, 500 in 2023/2024 and 1,600 in 2025/2026, while SUBEB recruited 1,500 teachers in the 2022/2023 session and another 1,500 in 2026. “Be rest assured that we will always stand with you and protect your dignity, and your place in our administration remains topmost,” Oyebanji said. He thanked teachers for their service and reiterated the government’s commitment to improving their welfare and working conditions. Earlier, the Commissioner for Education, Dr Bimpe Aderiye, commended the governor for his investment in the education sector, saying billions of naira had been expended across various levels. The state chairman of the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT), Lawrence Adedeji, and his counterpart in the Academic Staff Union of Secondary Schools (ASUSS), represented by Austin Bamidele, also commended the governor for his commitment to teachers’ welfare. They, however, appealed to the government to fulfil its promises on the payment of outstanding emoluments, stressing that the welfare and recognition of teachers should go beyond the annual celebration. “Celebration of teachers should go beyond just a day in October but every day,” they said. items.title: Inondations à Dakar: la menace persiste, le gouvernement active le plan d’urgence
items.description: Les fortes pluies qui ont frappé Dakar ce week-end continuent de peser sur la capitale. Plusieurs quartiers restent sous les eaux stagnantes, la circulation est toujours perturbée et de nouvelles précipitations sont annoncées. Face à la situation, le gouvernement a déclenché le plan d'urgence régional et renforcé son dispositif de veille. Dakar a gardé les pieds dans l'eau tout le week-end. Ce lundi, la situation demeure préoccupante. Autour du Premier ministre Ahmadou Alhaminou M. Lo, les ministères de l'Assainissement, de l'Urbanisme, de l'Intérieur, de la Sécurité publique, des Forces armées, de la Famille, des Infrastructures et des Transports ont fait le point. Les Finances et la Santé, dont les titulaires sont hors du pays, étaient représentées. Le constat est sans équivoque, la menace n'est pas écartée. « Nous avons passé en revue la situation liée aux fortes pluies de ce week-end », a déclaré le chef du gouvernement. De nouvelles précipitations sont à prévoir, selon le directeur général de l'Anacim, présent à la réunion. « Il y a de fortes probabilités de pluie pour lundi, mardi et mercredi », a-t-il indiqué. L'État se place en vigilance renforcée. « Le plan d'urgence régional va être déclenché », a annoncé Ahmadou Alhaminou M. Lo. Objectif, suivre au plus près l'évolution et intervenir rapidement dans les zones les plus exposées. Plusieurs points critiques ont été identifiés, l'avenue Malick Sy, l'autoroute à péage, l'avenue Philippe Maguilen Senghor et la zone de captage. Au-delà des routes inondées, c'est la continuité des services essentiels qui inquiète. « Nous restons attentifs à l'impact éventuel sur l'alimentation en eau et en électricité », a souligné le Premier ministre, assurant que des mesures préventives seront prises en amont. La circulation reste fortement perturbée dans plusieurs secteurs de la capitale. « Nous savons que la mobilité est difficile », a reconnu le chef du gouvernement, précisant que des opérations de dégagement ont été engagées depuis la veille pour un rétablissement progressif. Le gouvernement veut aussi renforcer l'information. Un dispositif d'alerte doit permettre aux habitants des zones exposées de suivre la situation en temps réel. Sur le plan humanitaire, l'assistance est déclenchée. Le ministre de la Famille, des Solidarités et de l'Action sociale a été instruit d'intervenir sans délai. « Les populations dans le besoin doivent être secourues dès aujourd'hui, à travers la distribution d'eau et de nourriture », a insisté le Premier ministre. Les moyens financiers suivront. « J'ai donné des instructions pour qu'à pied levé, les fonds pour tout appui ou toute intervention d'urgence soient disponibles », a-t-il déclaré à l'endroit du ministère des Finances. Pour coordonner les opérations, un comité de veille a été mis en place aux côtés de l'état-major. Il sera chargé de suivre l'évolution, de coordonner les interventions et de faire remonter les difficultés du terrain. « Je présente à nouveau mes condoléances aux familles attristées et je dis à toutes celles qui sont touchées notre compassion et celle du chef de l'État. Nous serons toujours à leurs côtés », a conclu le Premier ministre. Abdoulaye DEMBÉLÉ

items.title: Guinée-CEDEAO : À Conakry, Adjaratou Traoré plébiscite l’unité et le sursaut communautaire
items.description: À la tribune de l'Assemblée nationale de Guinée, lors de l'ouverture de la session ordinaire de la 10e législature, l'Honorable Adjaratou Traoré, deuxième Vice-présidente du Parlement de la CEDEAO, a pris la parole pour porter un plaidoyer vibrant en faveur de l'intégration sous-régionale. ​Mandatée par la Présidente du Parlement de la CEDEAO, Hadja Memounatou Ibrahima, l'élue ivoirienne a célébré le retour et la place stratégique de la Guinée au cœur de la famille ouest-africaine. ​« La Guinée est et reste un pilier de notre Afrique de l'Ouest » ​Dans une adresse aux accents fraternels et solennels, Adjaratou Traoré a rappelé le rôle historique du pays hôte : ​« Membre fondateur de la CEDEAO, la Guinée a participé dès les premiers jours à l'ambition d'une Afrique de l'Ouest capable de construire collectivement son destin. Sa position géostratégique, ses ressources et son potentiel économique la rendent tout simplement indispensable. » L'émissaire de la CEDEAO a également tenu à adresser une pensée chaleureuse au peuple guinéen, non sans réaffirmer que l'unité de la région repose avant tout sur une histoire et des aspirations partagées. ​ Sécurité, climat, jeunesse : Unir les forces face aux urgences ​Loin d'ignorer la réalité du terrain, l'oratrice a mis en lumière les défis majeurs qui menacent la stabilité des États de la sous-région, notamment la résilience face aux changements climatiques et la sécurité alimentaire ; la création d’emplois pour la jeunesse et l'accélération de la transformation numérique ; la gouvernance durable des ressources et la réponse aux menaces sécuritaires. ​« Aucun de nos États ne peut, à lui seul, apporter de réponse durable. Notre capacité d'action dépend de notre aptitude à traduire nos engagements communautaires en résultats concrets », a-t-elle insisté, appelant les parlementaires à faire preuve d'exigence et de pragmatisme. ​Une diplomatie parlementaire au service direct des citoyens ​Pour la deuxième Vice-présidente, l'efficacité de l'institution régionale ne se mesurera pas au nombre de réunions, mais à l'impact réel sur le quotidien des populations : la libre circulation effective des biens et des personnes, des opportunités économiques accrues et une sécurité consolidée aux frontières. ​En scellant cette rentrée sous le signe de la concertation technique et du dialogue continu entre le Parlement de la CEDEAO et l'Assemblée nationale guinéenne, Adjaratou Traoré a posé les jalons d'un partenariat renouvelé, axé sur la prévention des crises et la prospérité partagée. Un appel à l'action collective vivement salué par l'hémicycle.

items.title: Deputy Education Minister appeals to striking teachers to return to classrooms
items.description: Deputy Minister of Education Dr Clement Apaak has appealed to striking pre-tertiary teachers to return to the classroom while the government works to resolve their outstanding concerns. He said the government recognised the legitimacy of the teachers’ demands and was committed to addressing issues relating to their promotions, salary adjustments, allowances, rural and underserved community incentives, and conditions of service. Dr Apaak appealed Bolgatanga during the 5th Upper East Regional Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Awards ceremony, where 15 journalists were recognised for their contributions to journalism. He explained that the delay in implementing new salary scales and consequential allowances for nearly 80,000 teachers who had passed promotional examinations was partly because of the challenges in transferring the relevant data from the Ghana Education Service (GES) to the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department. The government had earlier agreed that promotions would be made automatic and that teachers would not be required to submit input forms, payslips and promotional letters before receiving their new salary scales and allowances. Dr Apaak said. He said the government had also agreed that the affected teachers would receive the new salaries and allowances with effect from January 2026, regardless of whether they wrote the promotional examinations in December 2025 or January 2026. On the proposed 20 per cent-plus salary incentive for teachers posted to rural, underserved and deprived communities, Dr Apaak said the government had assured the teacher unions that its implementation would begin next year. However, the government was working to clearly define which communities qualified as rural, underserved and deprived to ensure that the policy was implemented fairly. He said the issue also involved determining what would happen to a teacher’s entitlement when the teacher was transferred from a qualifying community. The Deputy Minister said the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission had been engaged to meet the leadership of the teacher unions, while President John Dramani Mahama had also directed a high-level meeting involving the Ministers of Finance, Labour Relations and Employment, Education and the teacher unions to continue the negotiations. “We want to encourage you to continue,” appealing to the teachers to return to the classroom as the government worked to resolve the outstanding issues. “We can be assured that what is due to them, no matter how long it takes, it will come for their arrears,” Dr Apaak said. Dr Apaak stated that the government was concerned about the impact of the strike on pupils and students, stressing that teachers remained central to the development of the country. He said the absence of teachers from classrooms could undermine efforts at providing quality education and urged all parties to work together to resolve the impasse. “Without the teachers, we would not be here,” he said, describing teachers as “the most important group of professionals.” The 5th Upper East Regional GJA Awards was held under the theme, “Beyond the Headlines: The Media’s Role in Promoting WASH for Safe Motherhood and Quality Healthcare.” The awards ceremony was supported by Lesken Enterprise Ltd, Myturn Limited, KacStone Records, Paga Youth Movement, NorthLite Solar Ltd, ActionAid Ghana, Afrikids Ghana, NABOCADO, Endswell Pharmacy, MTN, Alafia, WaterAid Ghana, Widows and Orphans Movement, Ghana Tourism Authority, Ghana Hotels Association and AquaBolg Natural Water

items.title: Mahama satisfied with Aayalolo contra-flow results – Ayariga
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama is satisfied with the initial results of the Aayalolo contra-flow system introduced to ease traffic congestion and improve the movement of commuters in Accra, Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs Mahama Ayariga has disclosed. According to Mr Ayariga, the pilot intervention has improved commuter movement during peak periods by allowing Aayalolo buses to operate against the normal direction of traffic on selected routes. Speaking at a Government Accountability Series on Monday, October 5, the Minister said the initial outcome has encouraged the President to engage key stakeholders on the future of the initiative. He said President Mahama is expected to meet stakeholders to review the pilot and determine measures to make the contra-flow arrangement a permanent feature of Accra’s public transport system. “One area of challenge in our increasingly congested cities is urban mobility. President John Dramani Mahama recently approved the trial of the contra-flow system that has enabled easy and rapid movement of several thousands of city commuters during peak hours using the Bus Rapid Transport Company, popularly known as Aayalolo buses. “He is satisfied with the initial successes achieved and has further scheduled a meeting of stakeholders in his office on Thursday, October 7, to review the trials and give appropriate directives on how to sustain the exercise permanently.” Aayalolo contra-flow pilot The Aayalolo contra-flow system was introduced on September 29 as part of government measures to address persistent traffic congestion and improve the movement of commuters across Accra during peak periods. Under the arrangement, Aayalolo buses are allowed to use designated lanes or routes in the opposite direction of the prevailing traffic flow during specified hours. The system is designed to provide commuters with a faster and more dependable public transport option, particularly during the morning and evening rush hours when traffic congestion is most severe. The initiative forms part of wider efforts to address urban mobility challenges in Accra, where rising traffic volumes have contributed to longer travel times and affected commuters’ access to workplaces, businesses and essential services. The stakeholder meeting scheduled by President Mahama is expected to provide an opportunity for authorities and relevant institutions to assess the pilot’s performance and consider the next steps for its continued implementation.

items.title: Au sein de l’AfD, on rêve d’annexer les Sudètes, une partie de l’Italie et l’Alsace-Lorraine
items.description: Des membres de l'Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), le parti d'extrême droite allemand, multiplient les « signaux irrédentistes » envers des régions ayant appartenu à l'espace germanophone, aujourd'hui situées dans d’autres pays européens. La démarche n'émane pas nécessairement de la direction du parti, mais aucune de ces prises de parole n'a pour autant fait l'objet de procédures disciplinaires à notre connaissance. En 2018, le groupe AfD au Bundestag a interrogé le gouvernement sur le travail de la « référente culturelle pour la Prusse-Occidentale, la Posnanie, la Pologne centrale, la Volhynie et la Galicie », dans une série de questions où il réclame un financement institutionnel pour les associations d'expulsés. En novembre 2019, Stephan Protschka, député de l'AfD au Bundestag, a participé au financement d'une stèle à Bytom rendant « hommage aux soldats allemands tombés pendant la Première et la Seconde Guerre mondiale, aux combattants des corps d'autodéfense et des corps francs, et aux Allemands de l'Est opprimés et assassinés ». En 2024, Alice Weidel avait déclaré avoir toujours refusé d’utiliser le nom polonais, Głubczyce, de Leobschütz, la ville d'origine de la famille de son père, dans l'actuelle voïvodie d'Opole. On remarque une accélération des provocations verbales en lien avec des « territoires perdus » depuis le début de l’année. Après que l'État russe a classé en mai la Landsmannschaft Ostpreußen, une association culturelle des expulsés de Prusse-Orientale, comme « organisation indésirable », l'AfD a dénoncé cette décision et a demandé au gouvernement allemand s'il en avait discuté avec Moscou. Le même mois, des élus de l'AfD en Bavière ont réclamé l'abrogation des décrets Beneš de 1945, qui ont servi de base légale à l'expulsion des Allemands des Sudètes de l'État tchécoslovaque reconstitué après sa dissolution par l'Allemagne nazie en 1938-1939. À l'occasion du congrès des Allemands des Sudètes, qui se tenait pour la première fois en Tchéquie, des membres de l'AfD ont défendu l'organisation de la manifestation malgré l'hostilité du parti tchèque d'extrême droite Liberté et démocratie directe (SPD), avec lequel l'AfD siège pourtant au Parlement européen dans le groupe Europe des nations souveraines (ESN). Le 12 septembre, à Termeno, lors du congrès du mouvement de jeunesse du parti Süd-Tiroler Freiheit fondé par Eva Klotz, Jean-Pascal Hohm, le chef de l'organisation de jeunesse de l'AfD (Generation Deutschland), a repris le slogan du parti en déclarant : « Le Sud-Tyrol n'est pas l'Italie ». L'Alsace, dont le territoire faisait partie du Saint-Empire romain germanique avant d'être rattaché à la France au XVIIe siècle, et qui a été annexée à deux reprises par l'Allemagne (en 1871 puis en 1940), a aussi fait l'objet de revendications. Un jeune militant de Generation Deutschland, la jeunesse de l’AfD, Marco Eggebrecht, a publié sur X le 9 mai une photo de lui accompagnée de la phrase : « Comment je te regarde quand j’entends : l’Alsace-Lorraine doit redevenir une possession allemande ». Wie ich dich angucke, nachdem du gesagt hast : "Elsass-Lothringen muss wieder in Deutschen Besitz übergehen." pic.twitter.com/XURCn7Be5X — Marco Eggebrecht (@MarcoEgge) May 9, 2026 Trois jours plus tard, le député européen Tomasz Froelich, un membre de l’AfD élu en 2024, a attaqué la France et dénoncé « sa politique agressive d'assimilation linguistique », ainsi que « l’hypocrisie » de l’Union en raison de sa critique de la politique chinoise vis-à-vis des populations ouïghoures. Im Elsass sprachen vor drei Generationen rund 90 Prozent der Bevölkerung Elsässisch – heute ist das eine aussterbende Sprache. Alles Folge der aggressiven sprachlichen Assimilationspolitik Frankreichs. Anstatt sich um den Schutz nationaler Minderheiten auf dem eigenen Kontinent… pic.twitter.com/Yp3g7mWxEj — Tomasz Froelich (@TomaszFroelich) May 12, 2026 Le 3 octobre, Jour de l'unité allemande, un dirigeant de Generation Deutschland, Luca Maurice Strauf, a décrit sur X la réunification comme « une victoire d'étape », en commentant une image qui inclut entre autres l'Alsace-Lorraine, le Luxembourg, l'Autriche mais pas la Silésie, la Poméranie et la Prusse-Orientale. Der Vorstand der AfD-Jugend, Luca Maurice Strauf, mit völkischem Revisionismus zum Tag der deutschen Einheit. Der 3. Oktober für ihn nur ein "Etappen-Sieg" vor der "großdeutschen Lösung". Mittlerweile wieder gelöscht, aber das lässt tief blicken. pic.twitter.com/Hx4IrotVdN — Gareth Joswig (@garethmetik) October 3, 2026 Il a depuis supprimé sa publication. L’article Au sein de l’AfD, on rêve d'annexer les Sudètes, une partie de l’Italie et l'Alsace-Lorraine est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Nearly 150m Africans live with mental health conditions — WHO
items.description: Agency urges greater funding, community-based care By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja Nearly 150 million people across Africa are living with mental health, neurological or substance use conditions, the World Health Organisation (WHO) has said, calling for greater investment in mental healthcare across the continent. The WHO Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, disclosed this in his message on the 2026 World Mental Health Day theme, “Lived experiences heard: real voices, real change.” Janabi said conditions including depression, anxiety disorders, and alcohol and other substance use disorders continued to affect individuals, families and communities across Africa. He also noted that stigma and discrimination remained significant barriers preventing many affected people from seeking help. According to him, major gaps persist in mental healthcare provision across the continent. “Only seven of the 47 countries in the WHO African Region are implementing comprehensive mental health integration into primary care,” he said. Janabi said average government spending on mental health in the region stood at only US$0.07 per person, compared with US$2.69 globally. He added that mental healthcare was often fragmented or concentrated in major urban centres, leaving many communities without access to appropriate services close to home. The WHO official called for people living with mental health conditions to have a stronger role in shaping policies and services designed to support them. He said the experiences of people with lived experience could help identify gaps in existing services, determine effective forms of support and ensure that care respected their dignity and rights. He said their perspectives, combined with clinical and public health expertise, could make mental health services more responsive and accountable. “Today, on World Mental Health Day 2026, under the theme ‘Lived experiences heard: real voices, real change’, I call for those directly affected by mental health conditions to be given a stronger role in shaping the policies and services that affect their lives. “Their experience can show us where services fall short, what forms of assistance make a difference, and how care can fully respect people’s dignity and rights. Listening to these voices is essential if we are to build mental health systems that are responsive, inclusive and effective,” Janabi said. He said WHO was creating more opportunities for people with lived experience to participate in mental health programmes across the African Region. Janabi noted that people with lived experience had served as key facilitators in the organisation’s Regional Mental Health Webinar Series and Mental Health Intercountry Learning Meetings in South Africa and Togo. He said the initiatives were developed and delivered in collaboration with the Pan African Network of People with Lived Experience of Psychosocial Disability, allowing affected people to contribute directly to discussions on mental healthcare. According to him, the approach was also reflected in the recently published Mental Health in Africa Investment Case by the WHO Regional Office for Africa. He said the report called for stronger community-based services, protection of human rights and sustained involvement of people who use mental health services. It also places the integration of mental health into primary healthcare at the centre of efforts to advance universal health coverage, he added. Janabi called for stronger national leadership and increased, sustained financing to address gaps in mental healthcare across Africa. He urged member states to establish formal and sustained mechanisms for involving people with lived experience in mental health decision-making. He also called on health professionals, civil society organisations and development partners to support the leadership of people with lived experience and help bring compassionate mental healthcare closer to communities. “As WHO, we are committed to working alongside Member States and communities to expand accessible and rights-based care throughout the Region. “Real voices can drive real change. Together, we can build mental health systems with those who use them, and ensure they respond optimally to the lives people lead,” Janabi said. items.title: Sahibzada Farhan to lead Pakistan T20I side against Sri Lanka; Shaheen Afridi retains ODI captaincy
items.description: Sahibzada Farhan will lead Pakistan in the three-match T20I series against Sri Lanka, while Shaheen Shah Afridi has retained the ODI captaincy for the subsequent tri-series involving England and Sri Lanka, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) announced on Monday. The T20Is will be played at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Oct 9, 11 and 13 before Pakistan host England and Sri Lanka in a seven-match ODI tri-series. The first three matches of the tri-series will be played in Rawalpindi, with the tournament then moving to Lahore for the remaining league matches and the final. Farhan, who captained Pakistan at the recently concluded Asian Games in Japan, takes over the T20I captaincy from Salman Ali Agha, who has been omitted from the shortest format. Salman, however, remains part of the ODI squad. The T20I squad also does not include Babar Azam and Shaheen, with the two retained for the ODI assignment. The 15-member squad includes uncapped all-rounders Razaullah and Mohammad Imran Randhawa. Razaullah recently made an impact on his Test debut against England, scoring 81 off 63 balls with nine sixes and taking four wickets. Randhawa, who also made his Test debut during the England series, has been included as a medium-pace bowling all-rounder. Maaz Sadaqat has retained his place after featuring prominently Pakistan’s Asian Games campaign, while Abdul Samad returns to the T20I side after last representing Pakistan in the format in March 2025. Hasan Nawaz has also been rewarded for his performances at the Asian Games, where he was Pakistan’s leading batter and finished the tournament as its highest run-scorer with 123 runs. He made 96 off 51 balls, including five fours and seven sixes, in Pakistan’s defeat by India in the final as the team settled for the silver medal. Fast bowler Naseem Shah returns to the T20I squad after last playing the format for Pakistan against Sri Lanka in February 2026. Shadab Khan, Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub and Abrar Ahmed are among the other established players in the squad. The 16-member ODI squad, meanwhile, retains a more experienced core under Shaheen, with Babar, Salman, Haris Rauf and Faheem Ashraf included. Hasan also returns to the ODI setup, and so does Razaullah. Wicket-keeper-batter Saad Baig, the former Pakistan Under-19 captain who scored more than 1,000 runs in the 2025-26 Quaid-e-Azam Trophy, has earned his maiden ODI call-up. Left-arm wrist-spinner Sufiyan Moqim is the other notable addition, while Mohammad Ghazi Ghori is also included as a wicket-keeper-batter. The PCB also announced a change to the coaching staff, with former Australia fast bowler Shaun Tait returning as bowling coach in a consultancy capacity. Tait previously served as Pakistan’s bowling coach during 2022-23 and will replace Ashley Noffke, who stepped down following the Asian Games to take up the head coach’s position with the Netherlands.

items.title: Kebbi NUT dismisses doctored video on education
items.description: Union defends Idris’ education record, salary reforms By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State chapter of the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT) has rejected a video circulating on social media, describing it as old, edited and doctored to create a misleading impression about education funding and teachers’ welfare in the state. The union, led by Comrade Zaki Sarki SK, said in a statement on Monday that the video contained what it described as false and unverified claims about the administration of Governor Nasir Idris and its performance in the education sector. Reacting to what he described as disparaging comments and allegations against the governor, Sarki alleged that the video was being circulated by individuals seeking to discredit the administration’s efforts in education and other sectors. The NUT leader said the union viewed the allegations as an attempt to incite teachers and other workers against the state government. He said the administration had taken steps to revive the education sector, which he described as having faced serious challenges before Governor Idris assumed office. Sarki said the governor inherited teachers earning less than the ₦18,000 minimum wage but subsequently reviewed their salaries to ₦75,000. He accused the originators of the video of deliberately omitting what he described as positive developments in the state’s education sector. According to him, the administration had constructed mega schools in four emirates, built more than 2,500 classrooms, recruited over 2,000 teachers and provided furniture and learning materials for schools. “To drag the image of a government to the mud that built mega schools in four emirates, constructed over two thousand five hundred classes, recruited over two thousand teachers, provided furniture and learning aids is, to say the least, a desperate attempt to smear the government’s hard-earned reputation,” he said. Sarki said the NUT remained supportive of the administration and would continue to work with it to improve education and deliver services to residents. “We at Kebbi NUT are solidly behind Governor Idris and we will continue to support him to provide dividends of democracy to the people of Kebbi State and we hereby condemn and reject the doctored video and its entire contents,” he said. He urged political actors to verify information before making claims about the state government, while calling attention to what he described as the administration’s achievements in the education sector. items.title: AI cannot replace Nigerian teachers – Alausa
items.description: … urges teachers nationwide to renew commitment to service, professionalism, patriotism …assures of Federal Government’s continued support By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Government has declared that the rapid rise of artificial intelligence and other technologies will not diminish the importance of teachers, insisting that the human judgement, encouragement and personal connection provided by educators remain indispensable to effective learning. The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, stated this Monday, in Abuja, while marking the 2026 World Teachers’ Day and the President’s Teachers’ and Schools’ Excellence Awards, PTSEA. Alausa, who spoke on the theme “Protecting and Advancing the Status of the Teaching Profession in a Rapidly Changing World”, said Nigeria must prepare teachers to harness emerging technologies without compromising the professional standards and values of teaching. His declaration came as education systems globally grapple with the disruptive impact of artificial intelligence, digital learning tools and rapidly changing skills requirements. According to the minister, while technology and AI can expand access to knowledge and help teachers tailor instruction to individual learners, machines cannot replace the human qualities at the heart of teaching. “These tools can help teachers reach learners and tailor instruction, but the judgement, encouragement and human connection of a skilled teacher remain indispensable,” he said. He stressed the need to equip educators with the knowledge and skills required to use emerging technologies responsibly and confidently, while protecting the integrity and professional identity of the teaching profession. Alausa described teachers as the foundation upon which every other profession is built, saying no doctor, engineer, scientist, entrepreneur or public servant could have attained professional success without the intervention of teachers. He said the annual celebration should therefore go beyond ceremonial recognition to sustained investment in the people responsible for preparing Nigeria’s next generation. “Every doctor, engineer, scientist, entrepreneur and public servant has benefited from a teacher and could not have become what they are today without teachers,” the minister said. “When we honour teachers, we honour the people who make every other profession possible.” He said teachers deserved professional respect, continuous career development, appropriate teaching resources, fair recognition and working conditions that would enable them to perform effectively. The minister said President Bola Tinubu’s administration had placed teachers and learners at the centre of its education reform agenda, with emphasis on improving learning environments, strengthening institutions, developing skills for a changing economy, improving education data and enhancing teacher welfare and professional development. According to him, the Federal Government would continue working with state governments and other stakeholders to improve the conditions under which teachers operate. He stressed that a child’s educational opportunity should not depend on geography, family income or circumstances. Whether in an urban school or a remote rural community, he said, every teacher should have the tools and institutional support required to help learners succeed. Alausa said the government could not undertake the task alone, noting that state governments, school leaders, professional bodies, organised labour, development partners, communities and parents all had roles to play in strengthening teacher preparation, development and recognition. The minister also used the occasion to call for renewed national respect for the teaching profession, saying the work of educators demanded more than one-day appreciation. He said the profession required sustained respect, investment and partnership throughout the year. “Your service calls for more than words of thanks on one day each year. It calls for sustained respect, investment and partnership through each day of the year,” Alausa told Nigerian teachers. He noted that millions of Nigerian children enter classrooms every school day with hopes, talents, questions and dreams, placing an enormous responsibility on teachers to transform their potential into opportunities. “That responsibility deserves our respect, support and national recognition,” he said. The minister also congratulated recipients of the 2026 President’s Teachers’ and Schools’ Excellence Awards, describing the recognition as a demonstration that teaching excellence deserves the highest national regard. He said the awards were designed to celebrate outstanding teachers, school administrators and schools for professionalism, innovation and leadership. Alausa urged the award winners to see their recognition not merely as a personal achievement but as a responsibility to inspire others and promote higher standards across the education system. He equally reassured teachers who did not receive awards that their contributions remained valuable to the nation. “Every lesson you prepare, every child you encourage and every young person whose confidence you build matters to Nigeria’s future,” he said. The minister’s message ultimately centred on the need to ensure that technological transformation strengthens rather than weakens the teaching profession. He said the government would continue to pursue reforms aimed at protecting the dignity of teachers, advancing their professional standing and ensuring that they were adequately equipped to operate in a rapidly changing world. Alausa urged teachers nationwide to renew their commitment to service, professionalism and patriotism, while assuring them of the Federal Government’s continued support. He said the administration’s education reforms were anchored on the conviction that “a child’s opportunities must not be limited by geography, family income or circumstance.” As Nigeria marked World Teachers’ Day, the minister said the nation must recognise that the future of millions of children remained closely tied to the quality, dignity and preparedness of the teachers standing before them in classrooms across the country. The post AI cannot replace Nigerian teachers – Alausa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ghana’s Rabiu Alhassan joins board of International Fact-Checking Network, IFCN
items.description: The Founding Executive Director of FactSpace West Africa, Rabiu Alhassan, has been elected to the board of the International Fact-Checking Network (IFCN), effective October 1. The IFCN at the Poynter Institute in the USA connects more than 170 fact-checking organisations worldwide to promote high standards, accountability in journalism and information integrity initiatives. “I hope to promote equitable partnerships in the face of major power imbalances in the information integrity ecosystem, highlight the severe lack of local-language AI moderation tools, particularly in this part of the world and help build sustained public trust in fact-checking,” Rabiu Alhassan stated in an interview. For a 3-year term, he will be representing Africa on the advisory board, which is expected to guide the IFCN through a time of uncertainty, innovation, and renewal, and will vote on all significant matters of IFCN direction, including approving verified member applications and renewals. As part of the exhaustive, multi-round voting process, there were regional and all-signatories global votes to determine candidates who had majority support (50%+1) of the voting community. Despite two available board seats for Africa, Alhassan emerged as the only finalist who cleared the 50%+1 threshold after the first round of voting in a contest that involved five other candidates – the IFCN will be expected to organise another election for the one extra Africa seat in 2027. Other newly elected board members include Ritu Kapur representing South Asia, Masato Kajimoto representing Asia Pacific, Europe will be represented by Thanos Sitistas. Latin America has two representatives, Daniel Bramatti and Olivia Sohr, Aws al-Saadi will be representing the MENA region, and Lori Robertson will be representing North America. Rabiu Alhassan’s board seat win is a testament to his continued contribution to the global fact-checking community, which has involved serving on several IFCN working groups over the years that have resulted in important outputs for global fact-checking efforts, including the IFCN Anti-Harassment Working Group, IFCN YouTube Working Group, and the IFCN Financial Sustainability Working Group. On the African continent, he has led FactSpace West Africa to become a recognisable contributor to the information integrity ecosystem, providing mentorship and training to several organisations and journalists, which culminated in the co-hosting of the 2024 Africa Facts Summit, the Africa Check-led annual Fact-Checking Conference in Accra, Ghana. Rabiu Alhassan is a journalist and media entrepreneur with 17 years of experience working across media channels – television, radio, print and digital platforms. After launching FactSpace West Africa in 2019 and guiding the organisation to become a signatory to the IFCN code of principles, which is the gold standard in fact-checking, he has invested in media innovation and the design of products at the intersection of technology and journalism, with a focus on information disorder. FactSpace West Africa has footprints in Nigeria, Ghana, Liberia, Sierra Leone, and The Gambia, contributing to localised efforts to tackle digital threats and the weaponisation of disinformation in the subregion. Alhassan holds an Erasmus Mundus master’s degree in Journalism, Media and Globalisation, specialising in Business and Finance from City St. George’s University of London (UK) and Aarhus University (Denmark).

items.title: El misterio de un escalador sin cuerda atrapado de noche en una pared y rescatado por un dron en Canadá
items.description: Ese escalador vasco llevaba años escalando en invierno las cascadas de hielo del Circo de Gavarnie y había sido testigo de varios rescates a cargo de los CRS franceses y su helicóptero. Los servicios de socorro en montaña de la diminuta localidad pirenaica no se limitaban a esperar una llamada de auxilio: solían observar las cascadas desde su puesto con potentes prismáticos, atentos a anticipar cualquier emergencia. Aquel día, hace cuatro años, no había más cordadas en el Circo, sumido en un frío silencio. Mientras escalaba, a unos 150 metros del suelo, escuchó un leve zumbido que no supo identificar. Después, se llevó el susto de su vida. “Buenos días”, escuchó en francés “le hablamos desde un dron en prácticas de la policía de montaña. Esperamos que pase un buen día de escalada”. Se escuchó un clic, como si alguien colgase un teléfono y el zumbido se alejó, dejando al escalador confundido. La llegada de los drones a los operativos de rescate en montaña promete optimizar aún más un trabajo sumamente complejo, pero hasta hace apenas unos días, la mayoría de los montañeros desconocían las posibilidades reales de estos aparatos. Un rescate de película en Squamish (Canadá) ha revelado al público su enorme potencial. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Flydubai : le Wall Street Journal révèle comment les contrôles ont échoué à empêcher l’attaque du copilote
items.description: Hamam al-Hammami n'aurait pas dû assurer de vols vers Israel. Selon l e Wall Street Journal , les pilotes originaires de pays sans relations diplomatiques avec Israel, comme Oman, ne sont pas autorises a y voler. Le copilote de flydubai avait neanmoins effectue plusieurs liaisons vers Tel Aviv avant d'attaquer son commandant de bord avec une hache de secours le 30 septembre. Une liste transmise, des controles qui n'ont pas suivi Flydubai avait bien envoye aux autorites israeliennes la liste des passagers et de l'equipage du vol 1073. Ces informations alimentent une base de donnees creee en 2023, notamment pour prevenir le terrorisme. Mais le ministere israelien des Transports n'avait jamais demande a consulter les listes, revele le journal. Il affirme qu'il ignorait pouvoir acceder a cette base. Charge de la securite des vols etrangers a destination d'Israel, il estime toutefois ne pas disposer des moyens de renseignement necessaires pour controler les equipages. « Les noms n'ont apparemment pas ete verifies comme il se doit, et il n'y a pas eu de controle approprie. C'est ainsi que nous en sommes arrives la », constate Eytan Ben-David, ancien directeur du bureau antiterroriste au sein du cabinet du Premier ministre israelien et ancien directeur adjoint de la division de la sûrete aerienne chez El Al. Un rapport confidentiel du controleur de l'etat avait signale, des mai 2024, des lacunes dans la surveillance des compagnies etrangeres et un partage mal defini des responsabilites. Un recrutement sans contact avec Oman Air En amont, une autre verification aurait pu alerter flydubai. Lorsqu'elle a recrute Hamam al-Hammami en fevrier, la compagnie a examine ses antecedents judiciaires, mais n'a pas contacte son ancien employeur, Oman Air, pour evaluer son parcours, selon le quotidien americain. Les autorites emiraties enquetent desormais sur les employes ayant participe a son recrutement. a Oman, les inquietudes remontaient a 2024. Apres avoir decouvert qu'il consultait des sites extremistes, les autorites omanaises l'avaient interdit de vol, envoye dans un programme de deradicalisation et affecte a un poste administratif chez Oman Air. Elles n'avaient cependant pas diffuse plus largement leurs craintes, rapportent les sources du quotidien. Le 30 septembre, le commandant blesse a reussi a ouvrir la porte du cockpit. Des personnes a bord ont pu intervenir, maîtriser le copilote et eviter le crash. Pour Eytan Ben-David, cette issue ne doit pas attenuer la gravite des defaillances : « Nous devons traiter cet incident comme s'il s'agissait d'une catastrophe. »

items.title: Argentina hit 7 as Burkina Faso land five hours before kick-off
items.description: Argentina produced a devastating display to thrash Burkina Faso 7-0 in a friendly overshadowed by problems surrounding the visitors’ trip to Buenos Aires. The African team arrived in Argentina just five hours before kick-off after a private flight from Morocco was cancelled because of a “technical failure”. Match organisers said several of Burkina Faso’s senior players then refused to travel, citing fatigue, which meant they fielded a young, inexperienced team at Estadio Monumental shortly after an 11-hour flight. Lautaro Martinez, Gianluca Prestianni, Nico Paz, Julian Alvarez, Franco Mastantuono, and Giuliano Simeone were all on the scoresheet for the hosts, while Moumoune Diallo netted an own goal. “What the Burkina Faso national team has done is truly commendable; it elevates football,” Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni said. “We try to respect them and are very grateful that they were able to come.” In a press release by match organisers, FIFA match agent Jairo Pachon said: “We would like to emphasise the commitment and dedication of the Burkina Faso federation and government. “Faced with an extraordinary situation, they worked to provide a solution that would allow their country’s representation to be maintained and give the footballers an important sporting opportunity.” ‘It will be an unforgettable day’ – Argentina prepare for Messi farewell Argentina’s talisman Lionel Messi did not feature against Burkina Faso, as he prepares for Tuesday’s friendly against Benin, which will mark the end of his 21-year international career. Messi announced his retirement from Argentina duty in August, following his country’s defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final and after saying he was considering his future in football after the death of his father, Jorge. The 39-year-old, who captained Argentina to World Cup glory in Qatar in 2022, has scored 125 goals in 207 appearances, making him the country’s all-time leading scorer and most-capped player. “I imagine Tuesday’s match will be very emotional for everyone, including Leo,” Scaloni said. “It will be an unforgettable day. It will be his day, and his teammates’ day, who also gave him his greatest footballing joy. I’m grateful to be able to enjoy it.” “I imagine that if there were five Monumental stadiums, they would be packed.”

items.title: Espagne : Une crise du logement fait tomber le Parlement, législatives anticipées le 29 novembre 2026
items.description: La XVè législature espagnole échoit finalement par anticipation et par la force d'une question qui s'est révélée cruciale : le logement. Contraint, le Premier ministre espagnol a annoncé dans la matinée de ce lundi 5 octobre 2026, la dissolution du Parlement et la convocation d'élections législatives anticipées le 29 novembre 2026 (alors qu'elles devaient se tenir à la mi-2027). Cette démarche radicale intervient après le rejet par le Parlement des décrets contre la crise du logement. Tout est parti vite, les éléments s'étant enchaînés pour aboutir à cette « démarche radicale » de proclamation d'un scrutin législatif anticipé programmé au dimanche 29 novembre 2026. En clair, une dissolution du Parlement. Cette décision fait suite au rejet, vendredi, 2 octobre, de mesures que le gouvernement avait présentées pour tenter de sortir l'Espagne de la crise du logement. Ce rejet a constitué un sérieux revers pour le dirigeant, ravivant les doutes quant à la capacité de son gouvernement, minoritaire, à se maintenir jusqu'aux législatives qui étaient prévues pour la mi-2027. La crise du logement qui touche l'Espagne a été récemment exacerbée après l'expulsion à Madrid, de Maricarmen Abascal, une femme de 87 ans. La situation a déclenché une vague de manifestations et l'installation d'un campement de militants en plein cœur de Madrid, explique actu.fr. MariCarmen est donc devenue le symbole de toute une génération de locataires ne pouvant plus assumer les hausses sauvages de loyer lors du renouvellement des baux. « Cette habitante de Madrid a été contrainte de quitter l'appartement où elle vivait depuis sept décennies, après le rachat de son logement par une société d'investissement qui souhaitait augmenter son loyer de 275 %. Samedi, des dizaines de milliers de personnes ont manifesté à Madrid et dans des dizaines de villes espagnoles pour réclamer un logement digne. Comme dans de nombreux pays européens, la pénurie de logements abordables constitue l'un des principaux problèmes sociaux en Espagne, où les plateformes de location touristique et les fonds d'investissement sont accusés de faire grimper les prix en achetant des biens immobiliers et en réduisant l'offre disponible pour les résidents », présentent des médias locaux, qui précisent également qu'après huit années au pouvoir, le Premier ministre Pedro Sánchez est déjà affaibli par des scandales de corruption impliquant plusieurs personnes de son entourage proche, notamment son épouse et son frère, ainsi que des collaborateurs-clés de son Parti socialiste. Face à l'émotion collective suscitée donc par cette affaire dite « Maricarmen Abascal », le gouvernement Pedro Sánchez a voulu légiférer (sans succès), en publiant deux décrets très ambitieux contenant des mesures comme l'encadrement des loyers, la limitation des baux à usage touristique, le durcissement des conditions d'expulsion ou encore l'interdiction de louer chaque chambre à un prix qui, cumulé, dépasserait celui de l'appartement entier. Désormais, les cartes sont à rebattre, et pour des observateurs, le Premier ministre Pedro Sánchez pourrait s'en tenir aux législatives anticipées du 29 novembre 2026 avec une majorité, en ce sens que des facteurs politiques et la configuration économique qui fait de l'Espagne « l'une des économies affichant la meilleure croissance en Europe » plaident, entre autres, en sa faveur. Mais, l'enjeu de ces joutes électorales n'étouffe nullement l'équation : comment résoudre cette crise de logement ? O.L. Lefaso.net Sources : actu.fr, equinoxmagazine.fr

items.title: At Moscow moot, Pakistan says terrorism remains core of Afghanistan's problems
items.description: Pakistan’s Special Representative for Afghanistan Mohammad Sadiq on Monday said that terrorism remained at the core of Afghanistan’s problems, reaffirming that Pakistan would continue to take “all appropriate measures” for ensuring the safety of its citizens, in accordance with international law. Sadiq made these remarks at the eighth meeting of Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan in the Russian capital. The moot brought together Afghanistan and other countries of the region to discuss the situation in Afghanistan and issues of regional concern, the Foreign Office (FO) said in a statement . Separately, Sadiq posted a transcript of his address at the meeting, according to which he told the moot that the roots of terrorism emanating from Afghanistan were in a “nexus between the Taliban regime and terrorist groups […] that operate with impunity on Afghan soil”. “The situation is worsened by external actors and spoilers who support proxies inside Afghanistan to target Pakistan and other countries in the region,” he added. Sadiq highlighted that five years into the Taliban rule in Afghanistan, “Pakistan faces the most serious security threat.” Over the last three years alone, he said, more than 4,700 Pakistanis had been killed due to terrorism emanating from Afghanistan. “No country would tolerate such a situation,” he remarked. “Thousands of innocent Pakistani civilians and security personnel have been martyred in the last few years. A result of terrorist attacks planned, financed, supported and carried out from Afghan soil. The Taliban regime is complicit in this. No responsible state can remain passive when its security is repeatedly undermined. and its people are viciously targeted.” The special representative said Pakistan’s counterterrorism operations were conducted in response to the terrorist attacks being perpetrated from Afghan soil. “These operations are precise, intelligence-based and defensive in nature. Pakistan’s actions are in exercise of its right to self-defence, to ensure the safety and security of its citizens. These actions are directed solely against the terrorist outfits based in Afghanistan that pose a threat to the region and beyond.” Sadiq continued that Pakistan had been, and would continue to take “all appropriate measures to uphold the safety and security of its citizens in accordance accordance with with international law, and based on the principles of necessity and as a measure of last resort”. “All measures taken by Pakistan constitute legitimate defensive actions against sanctuaries and bases used for planning, training and launching terrorist attacks inside Pakistan. “The scale and scope of our actions represent restraint, particularly in light of the severity of the challenge we face.” Sadiq said Islamabad desired peace in the region and had “remained patiently engaged” in political and diplomatic efforts aimed at addressing terrorism emanating from Afghan soil. “It is unfortunate that Pakistan’s numerous goodwill gestures and highly responsible approach were misconstrued, resulting in increased terrorist attacks from Afghan soil, with the active support and backing of the Taliban regime. “Pakistan reiterates its strong resolve and determination to uproot the menace of terrorism emanating from across the border. We call upon the Afghan authorities to end the impunity with which terrorist groups continue to operate from their soil,” he said. Sadiq also expressed hope that “countries in the region will work together to address the sources of instability in our immediate neighbourhood, with a view to achieving our collective objectives of regional peace, stability and prosperity”. “We expected the Taliban regime would take concrete and verifiable actions against those terrorist groups. Regrettably, they failed to act in complete disregard for the legitimate security concerns of Pakistan and other countries. We hope that the Taliban will honour their commitments made to the international community,” he said. Sadiq said Pakistan and Afghanistan were immediate neighbours having historical relations and fraternal bonds. “Peace and stability in Afghanistan is in the national interest of Pakistan.” Earlier in his address, Sadiq noted that the meeting was taking place at a “time of immense turmoil”. “The regional and global environment is fraught with challenges. Proliferating crises across the world, the ongoing conflict in West Asia, and disruptions in global energy markets have put unprecedented strain on our region and beyond. “At the same time, regional countries remain highly vulnerable to destabilising threats caused by terrorism, drug smuggling, illegal migration, and human trafficking,” he said. He noted that it had been five years since the transition in Afghanistan, with the Afghan Taliban taking the reins in Kabul in August 2021. This represented a “critical milestone” to assess the situation on the ground, he said. In the period after August 2021, Pakistan joined the regional countries in the efforts to help stabilise the situation in Afghanistan and address the humanitarian needs of people of Afghanistan, the special representative continued. “As a close neighbour, Pakistan engaged at the highest level, facilitated humanitarian relief efforts, and provided visas to vulnerable Afghans. Pakistan also extended trade and transit incentives to support Afghan economy, participated in regional initiatives and connectivity projects, and remained at the forefront of the efforts to facilitate Afghanistan’s integration into the international community.” These endeavours, he said, were driven by “our shared commitment to a peaceful, stable and prosperous Afghanistan”. “Our regional engagement had been central to assisting the Afghan authorities as they worked towards rebuilding their country.” However, he said, despite these efforts, Afghanistan stood at a critical juncture. “The country faces a deteriorating humanitarian crisis, and is grappling with multiple challenges driven by severe food insecurity, extreme climate shocks, water scarcity, and recurrent natural disasters and [a] permissive environment allowing terrorism to grow.” While it remained essential to call for sustained support, it was equally imperative to assess the progress towards resolving the legitimate concerns of regional states and the wider international community, Sadiq emphasised. “Nowhere is the lack of progress more evident than on the issue of counterterrorism, ensuring women’s rights and girls’ education, and promoting inclusivity. Continuing restrictions on women and girls, absence of any meaningful efforts to ensure broad-based governance, and the lack of progress on counterterrorism commitments not only impede Afghanistan’s long-term development and stability, they also threaten regional security and undermine our collective efforts towards regional peace and prosperity,” he said. Sadiq said the situation required careful reflection. “There is a need to ask whether the Taliban regime’s policies have advanced the collective objective of helping ordinary Afghans, and whether these policies have helped Afghanistan in responding to the legitimate concerns of the immediate neighbours,” he said. According to the FO statement, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov also attended the session and addressed the participating delegations. The consultations at the meeting focused on regional peace and security, counterterrorism, economic cooperation and connectivity, as well as continued engagement with Afghanistan, the FO said. It added that apart from Sadiq, the delegation from Islamabad included Ambassador to Russia Faisal Niaz Tirmizi, Ambassador to Afghanistan Ubaidur Rehman Nizamani and other senior officials. The Moscow Format is a Russia-led regional consultation mechanism that was initiated in December 2016. Cross-border terrorism and fraught Pak-Afghan ties As its eighth meeting takes place, Islamabad continues to urge the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say these repeated appeals have gone unheeded. According to a UN Security Council-mandated monitoring report — covering the period from Dec 16, 2025 to June 9, 2026 — Afg­han Taliban’s continued support for TTP has contributed to a rise in the frequency and lethality of terrorist attacks in Pakistan, even as Kabul has taken some initial steps to rein in the group. The report also points to growing operational and facilitation linkages among TTP, Al Qaeda, ISKP and BLA. Ties between the two neighbours have been strained in the past few years amid Islamabad’s concern over cross-border terrorism. On the night of February 26, following unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban from across the border, Pakistan launched Operation Ghazab lil Haq against terrorist hideouts. September witnessed another bout of conflict between Pakistan and Afghanistan. On Sept 21, in response to recent major terrorist attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan conducted “calibrated” airstrikes in the border region with Afghanistan against terrorist hideouts, with the government saying more than 28 terrorists were killed. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar described the action as part of Operation Ghazab lil Haq, which was launched on the night of Feb 26 in response to unprovoked cross-border firing by the Afghan Taliban. Days later, Pakistan shot down eight drones launched from across the border that had entered Pakistani airspace near the Torkham border and Kohat. It was also reported that the Afghan Taliban engaged in unprovoked firing the night before near Kurram as security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Pakistan. In retaliation to the drone incursion, Pakistan conducted “precision aerial and drone strikes” in 10 locations across Afghanistan. The Foreign Office (FO) said a demarche was also delivered to the Afghan side on account of an airspace violation by drones on Sept 23. The demarche was delivered on Sept 26, the FO spokesperson said in a statement. On Sept 25, the information ministry had also dismissed claims by the Afghan defence ministry of a Pakistani post having been destroyed near the Spin Boldak border — the frontier between Balochistan and Kandahar. Then last week, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said that Pakistan had the right to self-defence and “everything that is necessary will be done” in response to terrorism emanating from Afghanistan .

items.title: NPP’s choice of Kojo Bamba, is a rejection of ‘suit and big English’ – Mustapha Gbande
items.description: The election of Kwadwo Fosu Boadu, popularly known as Kojo Bamba, as First Vice Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) reflects the grassroots’ rejection of what the National Democratic Congress (NDC) Deputy General Secretary in charge of Operations, Mustapha Gbande, describes as “suit and big English” politics. Kojo Bamba was elected First Vice Chairman of the NPP after topping the party’s Vice Chairmanship contest with 3, 116 votes. Mr Gbande said the outcome of the NPP’s recent national executive elections demonstrates the preference of the party’s grassroots for leaders with strong connections to the base. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse , he described Bamba’s election as a reward for his grassroots activities, while arguing that the outcome also sends a message about the kind of leadership NPP delegates want. “The NPP has chosen a Delta Force commander over all of this. For a grassroots NPP person, it’s a reward. It’s a message to their desire for security and their disapproval of all this suit and big English,” he said. Mr Gbande further argued that the rejection of some former government appointees in the elections showed that NPP delegates were unwilling to accept attempts to blame party executives for the party’s electoral defeat. He said the development should also serve as a lesson to the NDC, warning that individuals who preside over a party’s defeat should not return to seek leadership while shifting responsibility to party officials who had raised concerns. Mr Gbande, however, raised concerns about Bamba’s election because of his reported association with the NPP’s Delta Force, arguing that the development could raise questions about the party’s position on political vigilantism. “If we are talking about invisible forces, it’s no longer about party; it’s about Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, isn’t it? Because of the election of Bamba,” he said. He added that if the issue was previously discussed in terms of groups or individuals associated with political vigilantism, Bamba’s election to a strategic party position could change the nature of the discussion. Mr Gbande acknowledged that the election of individuals with histories of association with political groups does not automatically mean a political party is endorsing violence, citing the NDC’s own history of political actors associated with groups such as the Azorka Boys. He nevertheless urged the NPP to consider the implications of the choices made in its latest national executive elections.

items.title: Éducation : la Fondation Orange Guinée et l’UNICEF signent un partenariat pour numériser 50 écoles
items.description: Dans le cadre du renforcement du programme de modernisation de l’enseignement guinéen, la Fondation Orange Guinée et le Fonds des Nations unies pour l’enfance (UNICEF) ont procédé, ce lundi 5 octobre 2026, à Conakry, à la signature d’un protocole de partenariat pour la numérisation de 50 établissements scolaires à travers le pays. Cet accord prévoit la prise en charge de 50 écoles réparties dans six régions du pays, notamment à Conakry, Kindia, Boké, Mamou, Labé et N’Zérékoré. Il prévoit également la formation de 500 adolescents aux sciences, aux technologies et au numérique, ainsi que l’attribution de 100 bourses et prix d’excellence à de jeunes lauréats. Selon la représentante de l’UNICEF en Guinée, Maddalena Bertolotti, cette initiative vise à faire du numérique un véritable outil au service de l’amélioration des apprentissages. « Cette ambition, c’est vraiment de mettre des équipements numériques à la disposition des écoles et de faire en sorte que ces outils contribuent réellement à améliorer les apprentissages des enfants et des jeunes. En Guinée, la pauvreté des apprentissages demeure un défi majeur. Trop d’enfants peinent encore à acquérir les compétences fondamentales en lecture, en écriture et en texte. Le numérique peut être un élément puissant pour améliorer la qualité et l’équité des apprentissages, mais le numérique ne suffit pas. Il doit servir aussi les priorités pédagogiques nationales et pouvoir aussi être utilisé dans les conditions réelles des écoles et des communautés. » Dans les zones les moins bien desservies, a-t-elle indiqué, l’apprentissage numérique repose sur plusieurs conditions essentielles : « L’apprentissage numérique repose sur quatre conditions indissociables. D’abord, c’est important d’avoir une source d’énergie qui est viable, c’est important d’avoir une connectivité qui est adaptée, des contenus qui sont validés par les autorités éducatives, qui sont aussi intégrés aux dispositifs nationaux, et aussi une condition très importante, c’est les enseignants. Il doit être accompagné et en mesure d’intégrer ces ressources dans les pratiques pédagogiques. Si l’une de ces conditions manque, les équipements restent inutilisés. Donc, ce n’est pas juste donner des équipements, mais c’est important d’assurer qu’ils sont utilisables. » Revenant sur les contours de l’accord, la représentante de l’UNICEF a précisé : « L’accord que nous signons aujourd’hui répond à ces conditions de manière intégrée. En matière d’accès, dans 50 écoles réparties dans 6 régions, et ce sera à Conakry, à Kindia, Boké, Mamou, Labé et N’Zérékoré, nous installerons des pôles d’apprentissage numérique alimentés par l’énergie solaire et qui seront aussi connectés. En matière d’apprentissage et de compétences, 500 adolescents seront formés aux sciences, aux technologies et aux numériques. Et 100 bourses et prix d’excellence, ils compenseront des jeunes lauréats. Cette initiative vise explicitement à réduire les disparités d’accès aux numériques éducatifs au bénéfice des écoles et des filles qui disposent aujourd’hui de grandes opportunités. » Pour Maddalena Bertolotti, cet accord repose sur trois aspects importants : « Cet accord a trois aspects très importants. Premièrement, la complémentarité des dons respectés, la conduite du ministère de l’Éducation. Ce partenariat s’inscrit dans les priorités du ministère de l’Éducation en matière d’amélioration des apprentissages fondamentaux et consommation du système éducatif. La Fondation Orange-Guinée apporte ses capacités techniques et logistiques, alors que l’UNICEF apporte son expertise pédagogique, son appui à la qualité des contenus et à l’accompagnement des enseignants, ainsi que des capacités de suivi et de méthode. Ce suivi est important parce qu’il ne porte pas uniquement sur le développement des équipements et l’accès aux ressources, mais va aussi mesurer l’utilisation des ressources et pouvoir vraiment contribuer à l’amélioration des apprentissages. » S’agissant des contenus de la plateforme, la représentante de l’UNICEF en Guinée a rassuré : « Les contenus sont validés par l’INRAP et le ministère avant d’être intégrés à la plateforme nationale. Et cela fait partie du cadre du programme décennal de l’éducation. C’est un point essentiel. Nous ne créons pas une solution numérique qui est parallèle, mais nous renforçons les dispositifs existants en cohérence avec la priorité du système éducatif. » De son côté, le directeur général et président de la Fondation Orange Guinée, Ousmane Boly Traoré, a soutenu : « C’est une occasion pour nous de manifester encore notre disponibilité à accompagner l’État dans son rôle régalien de formation, de préparation de sa jeunesse pour un meilleur futur pour la République de Guinée. » Avec l’Éducation nationale et des organisations comme l’UNICEF, le patron de la Fondation Orange Guinée a réaffirmé la volonté de son institution de mettre les outils numériques au service de la jeunesse : « Orange Guinée se veut un socle qui met à profit l’ensemble de ces outils numériques afin de contribuer à la formation des enfants, des jeunes en général, des filles. Et utiliser les moyens de la Fondation pour accompagner l’UNICEF afin de pouvoir magnifier ce rôle que nous voulons jouer auprès de la jeunesse en général. » Au nom du ministre de l’Éducation nationale, le directeur général de l’INRAP, Malick Bah, s’est réjoui de ce partenariat : « C’est un vaste programme qui démarre et notre plateforme va très bientôt embarquer ce nouveau support pédagogique. Donc, avec la Fondation Orange, j’ai apprécié vos discours en disant qu’il faut valider l’INRAP. C’est extrêmement important parce qu’il faut qu’on soit en phase avec les programmes, les manuels et tout ce qui est produit par Palindra pour l’école qu’il est. Donc nous, on ne peut que se réjouir de ce partenariat-là, ça va renforcer un peu ce que nous faisons avec l’UNICEF et j’avoue que nous sommes disposés à collaborer en matière de production de contenu pédagogique pour que tout se passe au bénéfice de qualité pour les enfants du pays. » Elisa Camara L’article Éducation : la Fondation Orange Guinée et l’UNICEF signent un partenariat pour numériser 50 écoles est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .
