items.title: Innovators urged to build low-cost, locally maintainable health solutions
items.description: The Ghana Medical Innovation Expo 2026 has ended with a call for Ghanaian innovators to design low-cost medical equipment together with health workers, from the drawing board, so that devices meet local needs and can be maintained by local engineers. The Director of the Institutional Care Division of the Ghana Health Service (GHS), Dr Lawrence Ofori Boadu, made the call at the Medical Innovation Expo 2026. Organised by Academic City University in partnership with Northeastern University, USA and the 4GBI (For Ghana Biomedical Innovation), the three-day expo was themed “Beyond the No-Bed Syndrome”. It brought together policymakers, health professionals, researchers, engineers and innovators. Bed management system In a speech read on behalf of the Director-General of the GHS, Dr Boadu said the Service was implementing an integrated bed management and referral coordination system to give ambulance crews real-time information on available beds and the capacity of health facilities to provide the required care. He said Ghana had about one hospital bed per 1,000 people, against the World Health Organisation (WHO) recommendation of five, adding that increasing the number of beds alone would not solve the problem. What was needed, he said, was a coordinated system that enabled patients to reach the right facility, with the appropriate equipment and skilled professionals, at the right time. He cited the case of a 29-year-old engineer who was knocked down at the Kwame Nkrumah Circle in Accra on September 5 last year. Although an ambulance reached him within minutes, he was taken from one hospital to another and died without being admitted. A committee set up to investigate the death found a “chain of delays”, including inadequate stabilisation and poor coordination among health facilities. Dr Boadu said the GHS had directed health facilities to stabilise emergency patients rather than turn them away, while thousands of health workers had been trained in basic life support. Bed tracking software has also been piloted at the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, Greater Accra Regional Hospital and Tema General Hospital, while bed management bureaus have been established in 10 regions. He said these initiatives were being integrated into a system that would give ambulance crews a dispatch console, referral coordination and a live view of available beds across the country. Local solutions Dr Boadu said the Bed Management Bureau would provide real-time information on bed availability, particularly at regional and teaching hospitals, to help ambulance teams decide where to send patients. He stressed that the challenge went beyond physical beds. “It’s not just a matter of beds, but again, with the skill, because when patients need care, it’s not about the physical bed, but it’s about the skill and then the equipment to manage that patient,” he said. Dr Boadu said the GHS was also working towards establishing a National Teleconsultation Centre to provide expert advice to lower-level facilities and reduce unnecessary referrals to major hospitals. He added that some imported equipment was difficult to maintain because the technology was beyond the capabilities of local clinical engineers. Innovation The Senior Research and Development Director of External Innovation at Johnson & Johnson MedTech, Dr Ibrahim Badejo, said innovation should start with unmet clinical needs and aim to solve real healthcare problems rather than simply producing sophisticated technology. According to him, the measure of innovation was its impact on patients and communities. Dr Badejo said Ghana could become an innovation hub if it developed solutions to local challenges and scaled them globally, adding that innovations should improve clinical outcomes, affordability and access, since solutions that patients could not afford or reach would have limited impact. He urged innovators to identify unmet needs, build multidisciplinary teams, validate their ideas early and work with hospitals, industry and government to scale successful solutions. Expo history The Vice-President of Academic Affairs at Academic City University, Dr Sena Agbodjah, said the BioInnovation Centre was established through a partnership involving Academic City, Northeastern University and Ghana BioInnovation, with a mandate to develop medical innovations to improve healthcare delivery. She said the annual expo brought together academia, industry, regulators and innovators to share their work and identify gaps that could guide future innovation. The first edition, held in October 2025 on the theme “New Paradigms in Healthcare Technology”, drew more than 200 participants. Dr Agbodjah said this year’s theme was chosen because the “no-bed syndrome” was a systemic challenge requiring solutions beyond simply increasing the number of hospital beds.

items.title: Frank Appiah Kusi, PhD: Governance Gaps, Transparency, and the Business of Football in Ghana
items.description: Football in Ghana is more than sports; it is a cultural institution and a national asset that unites communities, drives national pride, offers economic opportunities, and has social power. Yet, despite its significance, the governance of football in Ghana remains fraught with challenges. The Ghana Football Association (GFA), often at the centre of reform debates, has faced criticism for poor accountability, weak financial transparency, and declining performance of the national teams. The recent crunch meeting between the Ministry of Sports and Recreation and the GFA was hailed as a turning point, but reforms targeted only coaching, leaving behind youth football development, women football, fan trust, infrastructure and governance. More so, the exclusion of the National Sports Authority (NSA)—the statutory body mandated to oversee all sport in Ghana—raises critical questions about transparency and the business of football. This editorial explores the governance gaps in Ghanaian football, examines how transparency affects sponsorship and commercialisation, and draws lessons from African and European best practices to propose a path forward. The governance of football in Ghana is characterised by overlapping mandates, weak accountability structures, unilateral decision-makers, and orchestrated nuances. The NSA, empowered under the Sports Act, 2016 (Act 934), is mandated to supervise and coordinate all sporting disciplines (Sports Act, 2016). Its exclusion from the recent reform dialogue undermines its statutory role and creates opacity in football governance. Sponsors and investors thrive on accountability, yet the absence of the NSA weakens oversight and leaves the Ministry and GFA to operate in a bilateral arrangement that lacks independent checks (Akpalu, 2026). This governance gap is compounded by the GFA’s reliance on government bailouts while simultaneously claiming autonomy under FIFA statutes. Such contradictions create tension between national laws and international football regulations. The result is a fragmented governance system where accountability is diluted and transparency is compromised. Without clear oversight, sponsorship deals risk being negotiated in opaque corridors, leaving room for favouritism and mismanagement. Transparency is the cornerstone of football business. Sponsors, whether local or international, demand clarity in financial management and accountability in the use of funds. In Ghana, however, sponsorship structures remain opaque. Betting companies dominate football sponsorship, while major corporate brands such as telecoms, banks, and consumer goods firms remain hesitant to commit due to weak financial disclosure and lack of independent audits (Quansah, 2026). This narrow sponsorship base erodes investor confidence and diminishes fan trust. Fans question whether sponsorship revenues are being used to strengthen grassroots football, build and maintain infrastructure, cushion women football or simply to sustain short-term fixes. The lack of transparency also stifles innovation in football commercialisation, limiting opportunities for broadcasting rights, merchandising, and stadium development. As Ghana seeks to rebuild its football ecosystem, transparency must be prioritised to attract diverse sponsors and restore credibility. The exclusion of the NSA from football governance creates three major risks. First, it exposes sponsors to reputational damage, as they risk being associated with corruption or mismanagement. Second, it narrows the sponsorship base, leaving betting companies as the dominant funders while other industries avoid opaque structures. Third, it erodes fan trust, reducing merchandise sales, stadium attendance, and overall engagement with the sport. These risks are not merely theoretical; they have practical implications for the sustainability of football in Ghana. Without transparency, football cannot attract long-term investment, and without investment, the sport cannot develop the infrastructure and talent needed to compete internationally. Nigeria, even though presents with its own ups and downs, offers valuable lessons in football governance. The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has emphasised corporate governance codes and independent auditing of sponsorship revenues. By partnering with private auditors, the NFF has reassured sponsors and attracted diverse investments from telecoms, banks, and consumer brands (Ogunleye, 2025). This model demonstrates that transparency and accountability can unlock corporate confidence and expand the sponsorship base; however, corruption erodes this practice. South Africa’s Premier Soccer League (PSL) is widely regarded as a model of commercialisation in Africa. The PSL operates with transparent broadcasting contracts, diversified sponsorships across industries, and strong fan engagement strategies. This has made the PSL one of the most profitable leagues on the continent (Ndlovu, 2024). Ghana can learn from South Africa’s emphasis on transparency in broadcasting and diversification of sponsors, which ensures financial sustainability and fan loyalty. The English Premier League thrives on independent governance structures and financial fair play regulations. Sponsorship deals are publicly disclosed, and clubs are subject to strict auditing. This transparency attracts global brands such as Emirates, Nike, and Barclays, making the Premier League one of the most commercially successful leagues in the world (UEFA, 2025). Ghana can adopt similar disclosure practices to reassure sponsors and attract international investment. Furthermore, Germany’s Bundesliga emphasizes fan ownership through the 50+1 rule, which ensures community accountability. Clubs are required to maintain financial transparency, and sponsorships are diversified across industries. This model balances commercial success with fan trust, demonstrating that transparency and community engagement can coexist with profitability (Müller, 2025). Ghana can draw inspiration from Germany’s emphasis on fan engagement and accountability to rebuild trust in its football ecosystem. The experiences of Nigeria, South Africa, England, and Germany highlight the importance of transparency, accountability, and diversification in football governance. Nigeria’s independent audits build corporate confidence, South Africa’s transparent broadcasting expands revenue streams, England’s financial fair play ensures accountability, and Germany’s fan ownership restores public trust. Together, these best practices offer a roadmap for Ghana to reform its football governance and attract sustainable sponsorship. To address governance gaps and restore transparency, Ghana must adopt a multi-pronged strategy. First, a tripartite governance model should be institutionalised, where the Ministry of Sports and Recreation, NSA, and GFA come together. The NSA should be allowed to institute a committee of experts in collaboration with GFA and other sectors of relevance in national coach assignment. The old mantra of the Ministry working directly with GFA should cease. NSA should be empowered with strong leadership at the Director General appointment with someone who understands the tenets of sport management and the changing dynamics of sport business. In doing so, the influence of the Ministry on NSA should also cease to enable the latter function by law serving as oversight responsibility of sport federations in Ghana. This mandate should have the backing and support of the Ministry of Sports and Recreation and Parliamentary Select Committee on Sport – as policy makers of sport in Ghana. This would restore accountability and ensure that no single entity or federation dominates decision-making. Second, independent audits must be mandated, with annual forensic audits conducted by credible and trusted firms to reassure sponsors. Third, a transparency rule should be established between the NSA, GFA and clubs to publish sponsorship agreements and financial reports online, allowing fans and investors to track the use of funds. Fourth, Ghana must diversify its sponsorship base, attracting telecoms, fintech, and consumer brands by guaranteeing accountability. Finally, fan engagement must be prioritised, adopting Bundesliga-style community accountability to rebuild trust and loyalty. Football is more than a game; it is a national asset with economic, cultural, and social significance. To protect that asset, Ghana must harmonise its sports laws with FIFA statutes, empower the NSA to fulfil its mandate, and embed transparency into football business. By learning from Nigeria, South Africa, England, and Germany, Ghana can transform football into a sustainable industry that attracts sponsorship, strengthens grassroots development, and restores the Black Stars’ continental reputation. Governance gaps and transparency challenges must be addressed not as isolated issues but as integral components of football’s business ecosystem. Only then can Ghanaian football thrive in the modern era. Reference Akpalu, A. (2026, October 3). Reclaiming the soul of our game: A structural blueprint for a self-sustaining, accountable Ghana football ecosystem. Modern Ghana. Quansah, M. (2026, October 3). Beyond Queiroz’s exit: Ghana football needs accountability, reform — not another quick fix. Graphic Online. Sports Act, 2016 (Act 934). Accra: Government of Ghana. Ogunleye, T. (2025). Corporate governance and football sponsorship in Nigeria. African Sports Business Journal, 12(3), 45–62. Ndlovu, S. (2024). Commercialization of football in South Africa: Lessons from the PSL. Journal of African Sport Management, 8(2), 77–95. UEFA. (2025). Financial fair play regulations and their impact on European football. UEFA Governance Report. Müller, H. (2025). Fan ownership and transparency in German football. European Journal of Sport Governance, 15(1), 101–118.

items.title: Burkina Faso : Le Premier ministre inaugure un amphithéâtre de 500 places à l’IBAM
items.description: Le Premier ministre, Rimtalba Jean-Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a procédé, ce 5 octobre 2026, à l’inauguration d’un amphithéâtre de 500 places, intégré à un complexe R+2, au sein de l'Institut burkinabè des arts et métiers (IBAM) à Ouagadougou. Réalisé dans le cadre de l’Initiative présidentielle pour une éducation de qualité pour tous (IPEQ), l'ouvrage a été piloté par le Bureau national des grands projets du Burkina (BN-GPB). L'infrastructure a été bâtie suivant les normes en vigueur. Elle comprend un bloc amphithéâtre doté de trois loges aménagées pouvant servir de bureaux, ainsi que des espaces technologiques de pointe, à savoir une salle de vidéoprojection, une salle de vidéosurveillance et une salle de lecture aménagée sous les gradins. Le bloc pédagogique se compose, entre autres, de six laboratoires spécialisés, de six bureaux administratifs, d’un service de reprographie et de deux locaux techniques. Au niveau supérieur, le R+1 abrite deux salles modulables d’une capacité de 210 places chacune et deux salles de 80 à 90 places chacune. Quant au R+2, il comprend deux mini-amphithéâtres de 210 places chacun et deux salles d’une capacité de 90 places chacune. Cette inauguration constitue la deuxième du genre après celle de l’amphithéâtre de 1 000 places de l’Université Nazi Boni à Bobo-Dioulasso. L’ouvrage a été entièrement réalisé par des compétences nationales. Selon le coordonnateur de l’Initiative présidentielle pour une éducation de qualité pour tous (IPEQ), Dr Zakaria Soré, la concrétisation de ces infrastructures s'inscrit dans la vision du Président du Faso, qui ambitionne d’« inventer l'avenir » en révolutionnant le système éducatif. Pour ce faire, il a expliqué que l’IPEQ a été mise en place pour faciliter la synergie entre les départements ministériels, notamment ceux en charge de l'éducation de base, du secondaire et du supérieur. Il a insisté en indiquant que la réussite éducative repose sur une démarche collective, seule garante de la formation de diplômés dotés de connaissances et de compétences pratiques au Burkina Faso. « L’IPEQ crée les conditions dans lesquelles les établissements peuvent produire de la qualité. À travers ces infrastructures modernes, elle rappelle qu’il est aujourd’hui possible de former la jeunesse sur place et aux normes de l’excellence mondiale », a-t-il ajouté. Le Premier ministre a confié que l'ouverture de ce complexe d’amphithéâtres marque le début d'une série d'inaugurations. Il est également prévu, une dizaine d'infrastructures au cours de l’année académique 2026-2027. « C'est véritablement une infrastructure dont nous pouvons être fiers (…). C'est la mise en œuvre concrète de la vision du camarade Président du Faso, vision donc qui s'est matérialisée par la création de l'Initiative présidentielle pour une éducation de qualité pour tous », a-t-il ajouté. Il a rappelé que cette journée marque également la rentrée académique au plan universitaire. À ce propos, il a souligné la normalisation des années académiques qui n’a été possible que par l'acharnement du monde universitaire. Par ailleurs, il a salué le monde enseignant qui œuvre pour rendre possible la vision du Président du Faso. « Et le message que nous avons porté aujourd'hui, c'est de dire évidemment que tout ce qui se transforme sous nos yeux dans le cadre de la révolution progressiste populaire, c'est le fruit de l'effort du peuple burkinabè. Et nous devons rester concentrés, comme le camarade Président du Faso l'a dit, et avancer dans l'ordre et dans la discipline pour amplifier ces acquis et faire en sorte évidemment que nous puissions transformer de façon structurelle tous les secteurs de la vie des Burkinabè, y compris évidemment les ordres d'enseignement » a-t-il invité. Au nom de ses camarades Eva Benjamine Kazienga, représentante des étudiants, a exprimé sa gratitude envers le Président du Faso pour l'obtention de ces nouveaux locaux. Ils leur permettront d'élever le niveau des formations et de la recherche. Aussi, ils se sont engagés à faire preuve de civisme et de responsabilité, et à œuvrer pour le développement du Burkina Faso. Cheick Habib Désiré BAYILI Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : Le Premier ministre inaugure un amphithéâtre de 500 places à l’IBAM est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Israel's deepening diplomatic isolation after 3 years of genocide in Gaza
items.description: After three years of Israel’s genocide in Gaza that has killed tens of thousands, Tel Aviv’s relations with its traditional Asian allies have increasingly fractured, deepening its diplomatic isolation. A recent illustration of that isolation came at the UN General Assembly late last month, where Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cut a lonely figure as scores of delegates walked out of his speech. The departing delegates included representatives from Asian nations such as Pakistan, Malaysia, Indonesia and Bangladesh. Here is a look at how Asian countries have responded to Israel and the Gaza war. Delegates attend Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s address during the 81st United Nations General Assembly as empty seats are seen in the General Assembly hall at UN headquarters in New York City, US, September 24. — Reuters East Asia Israel has faced strong state-level criticism from its longtime East Asian allies, such as Japan and South Korea. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi opposed US sanctions against International Criminal Court (ICC) President Tomoko Akane, who sought an arrest warrant for Netanyahu over alleged war crimes in Gaza. Takaichi reaffirmed Tokyo’s consistent support for the ICC during the UN General Assembly, pushing back against pressure from the US, and saying that the country takes the US sanctions against Akane “very seriously.” Washington sanctioned Akane, the first Japanese national to head the ICC, in August, accusing the court of encroaching on state sovereignty. Japanese Judge Tomoko Akane, President of the International Criminal Court (ICC), delivers a speech during a press conference at the Japan National Press Club in Tokyo on June 14, 2024. —AFP/File With Seoul, tensions began in April after South Korean President Lee Jae Myung shared a video on social media alleging that Israeli soldiers abused a Palestinian child and then threw him off a rooftop. Lee said it was necessary to determine the authenticity of the video and assess what actions were taken, stressing the seriousness of the allegations. “Wartime homicide is no different from matters that we take issue with, such as the forced [enslavement of] comfort women, and the massacre of Jewish people,” he said. The issue of “comfort women” refers to the sexual enslavement of thousands of women and girls, many of them Korean, by the Imperial Japanese Army during World War II. Israel strongly criticised Lee for posting the video, calling it “unacceptable.” Israel’s Foreign Ministry claimed that Lee relied on a “fake account” and had revived an incident from 2024 that had already been investigated. The ministry also accused Lee of trivialising the massacre of Jews on the eve of Holocaust Remembrance Day in Israel. China, which has long supported a two-state solution, continued to reiterate its call. President Xi Jinping said the two-state solution is the “right direction” for resolving the longstanding Palestine issue. South and Southeast Asia Sri Lanka, one of the first countries to recognise the State of Palestine, called at the UN General Assembly for the “early” recovery and reconstruction of Gaza, reiterating its support for Palestinians’ “inalienable” rights and a two-state solution. “Recovery and reconstruction of Gaza must be an early priority,” Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath said in his address, adding that Colombo supports resolving the Palestine issue in line with the 1967 borders. Pakistan, a member of the Gaza Board of Peace, also reiterated its “unwavering” support for the Palestinian people and the establishment of an independent State of Palestine based on the pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital. Addressing the UN General Assembly, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said that Palestine must also be granted full membership in the UN. India, for its part, continued to pursue its strategy of maintaining diplomatic and strategic ties with Israel while continuing to express traditional support for a two-state solution and Palestinian statehood. India under Prime Minister Narendra Modi has significantly deepened its strategic relationship with Israel, including through Modi’s February meeting with Netanyahu , when the two countries elevated their ties to a “Special Strategic Partnership”. According to Jatin Desai, a Mumbai-based political analyst, India has historically stood with the Palestinian people. He said India’s position was clear even before the establishment of Israel.​​​​​​​ Thailand, which has maintained long-standing ties with Israel, continues to cooperate closely with Israel, particularly in agriculture and education. Every year, around 100,000 Israeli tourists travel to Thailand, and thousands of Thai workers, both skilled and unskilled, are employed in Israel. The country is also a popular destination for Thai students pursuing academic studies. Bangkok established diplomatic relations with Israel in 1954, while it officially recognised Palestine in 2012. Pacific nations In January, US President Donald Trump, as chair of the Board of Peace, invited Australia, Vietnam and Thailand to join the international body. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Canberra would consider the offer, though no decision had so far been taken. “We’ve received correspondence from the president that arrived, I think, last night. That’s something we haven’t had time to consider. We’ll consider all of these approaches respectfully and through our proper processes,” Albanese said after receiving the invitation. Thailand said it was reviewing the details of the offer, while Vietnam’s Communist Party General Secretary To Lam accepted Trump’s invitation to join the Gaza Peace Council and “affirmed Vietnam’s readiness to participate as a founding member state of the council”. A Palestinian young man stands amid the debris of Al-Hassayna family company’s warehouse, damaged during Israeli bombardment, in Gaza City on September 28, 2026. — Reuters New Zealand, which did not join neighbouring Australia and other European nations in recognising the State of Palestine last year, said recognition of Palestinian statehood is “inevitable”. In his final speech as Wellington’s foreign minister in the incumbent government earlier this month, Winston Peters said his decision in 2025 not to join most other UN member states in recognising Palestine was an example of truly independent foreign policy. The Pacific, a cluster of small island nations, has provided Israel with a bloc of supportive voices in international forums, even as global criticism intensifies and more countries move to recognise Palestine. Fiji further strengthened ties with Israel in September 2025 by opening a new embassy in Jerusalem. Days earlier, it abstained in a UN vote on a two-state solution. Like many of its neighbours, Fiji does not recognise Palestine. Papua New Guinea followed a similar path. In September 2023, it also opened an embassy in Jerusalem and has since repeatedly opposed calls for a ceasefire at the UN. The country continues to reject recognition of Palestinian statehood. Nauru has long been a loyal supporter of Israel. It recognised Jerusalem as Israel’s capital in 2019 and, in September last year, voted against a resolution backing a two-state solution. Palau and Micronesia have consistently voted in line with Israel at the UN. Samoa signed a visa-waiver deal in 2019 but took a slightly different line in September last year, when it abstained in the two-state resolution. Still, like most of its neighbours, it has not recognised Palestine. Other Pacific nations such as Vanuatu, the Marshall Islands, Kiribati, the Solomon Islands, Tuvalu and Tonga maintain diplomatic relations with Israel, regularly support it at UN forums and do not recognise Palestine. Tonga and Israel signed a visa-waiver agreement in 2010, while Vanuatu and the Marshall Islands have consistently backed Israel in UN votes.

items.title: World Teachers’ Day: Obi demands better welfare
items.description: … Calls for priority funding of education, infrastructure Former Anambra State governor and presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, has called for improved welfare, working conditions and professional dignity for Nigerian teachers. Obi made the call in a message posted on his X platform on Monday to mark World Teachers’ Day. He described teaching as one of the most important professions in any society, saying teachers play a critical role in shaping minds, nurturing character and preparing future citizens, professionals and leaders. According to him, the quality of teachers will significantly determine the quality of Nigeria’s human capital and, ultimately, the country’s future. “I salute our teachers for their resilience, dedication, and immense sacrifices, often made under difficult socio-economic conditions,” Obi said. He urged governments to do more to improve teachers’ welfare, ensure prompt payment of their salaries, provide conducive working environments and equip them with the tools required for effective teaching. “The dignity of the teaching profession must be restored,” he said. Obi also called for greater investment in education, arguing that Nigeria could not effectively tackle out-of-school children, unemployment, poverty and underdevelopment without sustained investment in the sector. He said education should receive greater priority in national planning and budgeting, with particular attention given to teachers and educational infrastructure. “To every Nigerian teacher, I thank you for your service and for continuing to build our nation, one child at a time. Please remain steadfast and hopeful,” he said. Obi expressed optimism that the Nigeria Nigerians desire was achievable, saying building such a country must begin with investment in its people. “With improved education, a new Nigeria that will be okay if possible,” he added. The post World Teachers’ Day: Obi demands better welfare appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Manhyia South MP charged with conspiracy, financial loss and money laundering
items.description: The Office of the Attorney-General has filed three criminal charges against Manhyia South MP Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah over alleged financial misconduct in his handling of a legal case involving SIC Life Savings & Loans Company Limited. The charges, filed at the High Court’s Specialised Jurisdiction Division in Accra on October 3, 2026, include conspiracy to commit a crime, intentionally causing financial loss to a public body and money laundering. According to the charge sheet, the State alleges that Mr Awuah, while acting as a lawyer for SIC Life, conspired with the company’s then Managing Director in 2024 to intentionally dissipate GH¢9.85 million belonging to the company. The second count alleges that he intentionally caused SIC Life to suffer a financial loss of GH¢9.85 million in the course of a business transaction. The third count alleges that Mr Awuah transferred GH¢1 million to the then Managing Director of SIC Life, knowing that the money had been acquired through crime and with the purpose of assisting the recipient to evade the legal consequences of an offence. How the case arose The facts accompanying the charge sheet state that Mr Awuah is the Senior Partner of Sarkodie Baffour Awuah & Partners, which was engaged by SIC Life in May 2020 to recover a debt of GH¢6.3 million from Equity Savings and Loans Limited. Under the terms of engagement, SIC Life was to pay the law firm 15% of the principal sum claimed as professional fees, together with 1% for expenses. In July 2022, the High Court’s Commercial Division entered summary judgment in favour of SIC Life against Equity in the sum of GH¢10.86 million. A 31.93-acre parcel of land belonging to Equity at Adamorobe, Oyibi, was subsequently attached in December 2023 in execution of the judgment. The facts state that a revised judgment dated May 28, 2024, increased the judgment debt to GH¢14.85 million, including interest and costs. The land had a reserve price of GH¢25 million. The State alleges that while the property was under attachment, Equity purportedly sold it to Eco Swiss Investment Limited on March 14, 2024, for GH¢21.76 million. Investigators, according to the charge sheet, found that Eco Swiss had not been incorporated at the time it purportedly acquired the property. The State further alleges that Mr Awuah was instrumental in arranging the transaction. The settlement By July 2024, Eco Swiss had paid only GH¢5 million of the purchase price and had filed a notice challenging the attachment, causing the auction to stall. On July 18, 2024, SIC Life, Equity and Eco Swiss entered into Terms of Settlement under which SIC Life agreed to accept GH¢5 million from Eco Swiss in full and final settlement of the revised GH¢14.85 million judgment debt. According to the prosecution’s case, the settlement terms also provided for the payment of 15% of the original judgment debt to Mr Awuah and his law firm as legal fees, amounting to GH¢2.2 million. Eco Swiss was also required to pay GH¢1 million in auctioneer’s fees. The State alleges that the Managing Director of SIC Life signed the settlement terms in conspiracy with Mr Awuah and that investigators found no record of prior approval for the arrangement. Alleged GH¢1m transfer The charge sheet further states that after receiving the purported legal fees, Mr Awuah issued a cheque for GH¢1 million to the then Managing Director of SIC Life on November 11, 2024. The prosecution alleges that the amount represented almost half of the purported legal fee paid to the lawyer. According to the facts, Mr Awuah has not told investigators the purpose of the GH¢1 million transfer. MP’s detention Mr Awuah voluntarily surrendered to the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) on October 1, 2026, following a High Court warrant issued on September 30. He spent the night in custody and was expected to be arraigned before a weekend court. The charge sheet was subsequently filed on October 3, with the MP expected to appear before the High Court’s Specialised Jurisdiction Division. Parliament has expressed concern over his continued detention, with Speaker Alban Bagbin calling for restraint and fairness in the exercise of coercive powers. What next? Mr Awuah is expected to be arraigned before the High Court’s Specialised Jurisdiction Division in Accra, where the court will also consider any application for bail. The allegations contained in the charge sheet are yet to be proven in court. Mr Awuah is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

items.title: Food Security: Buffer Stock CEO calls for more investment in Agri-Tech
items.description: The CEO of the National Food Buffer Stock Company (NAFCO), George Abradu-Otoo, has called for increased investment in technology to strengthen food security interventions across Africa. According to him, greater deployment of technology in agriculture is critical to achieving the continent’s food sufficiency goals. Mr Abradu-Otoo made the call at a forum on biotechnology, ecosystems and food security during the 2026 International Forum on Industry and Technologies for Humans in Gelendzhik, Russia. The two-day event, known as BIOPROM 2026, brought together scientists, policymakers, government officials and trade experts to examine the impact of biotechnology on health, science and food security. Mr Abradu-Otoo identified Artificial Intelligence, drones, climate sensors, and advanced irrigation systems as technologies that could help improve agricultural productivity and strengthen food self-sufficiency. He also commended the Ghanaian government for strengthening public policy on agriculture through initiatives aimed at stimulating and increasing production, including the Agriculture for Economic Transformation programme. The forum was opened by Russia’s Deputy Prime Minister, Denis Manturov, who reiterated the government’s commitment to addressing challenges contributing to food insecurity in the region. Mr Abradu-Otoo subsequently held discussions with Mr Manturov and other Russian government officials on issues related to agriculture, technology and food security.

items.title: Upper parts of country likely to see rainy, windy conditions from Oct 6-7
items.description: The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) on Monday predicted heavy rains, strong winds and thunderstorms, with isolated hailstorms, in the upper parts of the country over the next two days. In a press release, the Met Office said a westerly wave was likely to enter the upper parts of the country tonight and was expected to persist until Oct 7 (Wednesday). Under the influence of this weather system, the PMD predicted rain, windstorms and thunderstorms, with isolated hailstorms, in various locations in Gilgit-Baltistan (GB), Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) and Punjab as well as the Islamabad region. In KP, “rain-windstorm/thunderstorm” were expected to begin from Monday night in Dir, Chitral, Swat, Kohistan, Shangla, Battagram, Mansehra, Abbottabad, Haripur, Buner, Malakand, Bajaur, Mohmand, Kohat, Peshawar, Charsadda, Nowshera, Mardan, Swabi, Khyber, Orakzai, Kurram, Hangu, Lakki Marwat, Karak, Bannu, Dera Ismail Khan and Waziristan. They are predicted to last until Oct 7 (Wednesday), the PMD said. In Kashmir, rain and hail were expected to fall during the next two days in isolated places, including Neelum Valley, Muzaffarabad, Rawalakot, Poonch, Hattian, Bagh, Haveli, Sudhanoti, Kotli, Bhimber and Mirpur. In GB, they were likely in Diamer, Astore, Ghizer, Skardu, Hunza, Gilgit, Ghanche and Shigar during the same period. For Punjab, the PMD forecast “rain-windstorm/thunderstorm” on Oct 6 and Oct 7 at isolated places in Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Murree, Galliyat, Attock, Chakwal, Jhelum, Mandi Bahauddin, Gujrat, Gujranwala, Hafizabad, Wazirabad, Lahore, Kasur, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Narowal, Mianwali, Khushab, Sargodha, Jhang, Toba Tek Singh and Faisalabad. While “mainly hot and dry weather” was likely to prevail in Sindh and Balochistan, the PMD noted that rain-windstorms and thunderstorms were also expected at isolated places in Balochistan’s Zhob, Barkhan and Musakhel on Tuesday evening and night. The Met Office warned that windstorms, hail and lightning could damage weak structures such as roofs and walls of kutcha houses, electric poles, billboards, vehicles and solar panels. It also noted that daytime temperatures were likely to drop by two to four degrees Celsius during the forecast period. “Farmers are advised to manage their crop activities keeping in view the weather conditions,” the press release stated, also calling on all relevant authorities to remain vigilant and take the necessary measures to avoid untoward situations. A fresh spell of rain hit the country last month, particularly affecting Rawalpindi as inundated roads and knee-deep water at certain points exposed the city’s poor drainage system. Islamabad and Rawalpindi received another burst of heavy rain at the end of September, with civic departments in the garrison city placed on high alert. Earlier that month, KP also witnessed rain as heavy downpours lashed Mohmand, damaging and flooding roads and creating difficulties for residents. Rain coupled with strong winds and dust had also damaged vegetable and maize crops in Bajaur district, but no casualties were reported.

items.title: Nigeria : le crash d’un avion militaire fait 32 morts dans le sud du pays
items.description: Un aeronef de l'armee de l'air nigeriane (NAF) s'est ecrase dans la region d'Igbokoda, dans l'etat d'Ondo, dans la matinee du 5 octobre, tuant ses sept membres d'equipage et ses 25 passagers, selon le ministre de l'Aviation et du Developpement aerospatial, Festus Keyamo, qui a confirme l'information sur son compte X. Le ministre s'est appuye sur les informations fournies par les controleurs aeriens concernant la disparition d'un avion militaire de type ATR-42, immatricule NGR 931, qui faisait route de Benin City a Lagos. Le contact radio avec l'appareil a ete perdu vers 9h13, a-t-il precise, ajoutant que toutes les tentatives pour le retablir s'etaient averees infructueuses. L'armee evoque une « mission de routine » Le ministre a fait remarquer que le controle et la reglementation des aeronefs militaires ne relevaient pas de la competence de son ministere ni de l'Autorite nigeriane de l'aviation civile (NCAA). Dans un communique, le directeur des relations publiques et de l'information de la NAF, Ehimen Ejodame, a indique que l'avion effectuait une « mission de routine » lorsque l'incident s'est produit, rapportent des medias locaux. Ouverture d'une enquete Le responsable des relations publiques de la police de l'etat d'Ondo, le commissaire adjoint Abayomi Jimoh, a lui aussi reconnu le crash et a annonce l'ouverture d'une enquete, ajoutant que « les details entourant l'incident sont encore en cours d'elucidation, les efforts se poursuivant pour etablir les circonstances exactes ».

items.title: Nigeria may crash chaotically under Atiku – Babachir Lawal says he’d rather back Tinubu
items.description: By Sekinat Osundiji Former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Babachir Lawal, has said he would rather support President Bola Tinubu than former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, arguing that an Atiku presidency could lead to a “chaotic” crash. Lawal made the remarks during an interview on the Naija Unfiltered Podcast , while explaining his opposition to Atiku’s presidential ambition ahead of the 2027 election. “I’d rather go with Bola than Atiku because when Nigeria crashes with Bola, it might be an orderly crash, but with Atiku it would be a chaotic one,” Lawal said. Asked why he held that view, the former SGF replied, “Because he’s not a good man.” Lawal said his position was influenced by his previous experience working with Atiku, although he had initially considered supporting the former vice president because of what he described as the worsening situation in northern Nigeria. “I wanted to work for Atiku. I had the belief that the North, the way we are suffering, we should not surrender the presidency, that at least our own man will not, if nothing else, stop the decline we are in,” he said. He, however, said his experience working with Atiku eventually changed his mind, alleging that the former vice president often issued instructions and later reversed them after consulting other people. “Everything you do with him, there’s chaos,” Lawal said. “He will call you and tell you, ‘Do this,’ and then you do it, then front you are back.” Lawal also alleged that disagreements over political appointments contributed to the confusion, claiming that decisions reached with Atiku were sometimes altered after interventions by others. The former SGF further disclosed that Atiku had previously asked him to persuade former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, to accept the position of running mate ahead of the 2027 election. According to Lawal, Atiku proposed serving one term before pursuing a constitutional amendment to make the presidency a single six-year term. He said Atiku also proposed that presidential rotation should subsequently begin with the South-East and North-Central zones. Lawal said he approached Obi because of his relationship with the former Anambra governor, but Obi declined the proposed arrangement. “He says his survey shows him that they are unlikely to win if he pairs with Atiku,” Lawal quoted Obi as saying. According to Lawal, Obi subsequently indicated that he would rather not contest than join a ticket he believed would lose. He said he later conveyed Obi’s position to Atiku and consulted some prominent Igbo figures in an effort to persuade Obi, but the attempt did not succeed. Lawal’s comments come amid ongoing discussions among opposition figures over possible political alliances ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The post Nigeria may crash chaotically under Atiku – Babachir Lawal says he’d rather back Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Dakar zéro inondation à l’horizon 2050 (Khouraichi Thiam)
items.description: Les fortes pluies enregistrées ces derniers jours à Dakar et dans plusieurs régions du Sénégal doivent nous interpeller collectivement. J’ai d’abord une pensée pour toutes les familles touchées par ces intempéries et adresse mes sincères condoléances aux familles endeuillées, notamment à la suite des pertes en vies humaines enregistrées aux Parcelles Assainies, à l’Unité 7. Au-delà de l’émotion et de la solidarité qui doivent accompagner chaque situation d’urgence, ces événements nous imposent une question fondamentale. La situation que nous vivons doit également être replacée dans un contexte mondial marqué par des dérèglements climatiques de plus en plus visibles. Les épisodes de pluies extrêmes et d’inondations touchent aujourd’hui des territoires très différents : l’Espagne, le Mexique, la Thaïlande, la Grèce, la Malaisie, mais aussi de nombreux autres pays. En Espagne, les épisodes de pluies extrêmes ont notamment provoqué des inondations majeures et de lourds dégâts ; des travaux scientifiques récents ont montré que le réchauffement climatique avait renforcé l’intensité des précipitations lors des inondations catastrophiques de Valence en 2024. En Thaïlande, les fortes pluies de septembre 2026 ont affecté des dizaines de provinces, y compris Bangkok, avec des conséquences importantes sur les populations, les infrastructures et l’activité économique. La Malaisie est également fortement exposée aux inondations, qui constituent l’un de ses principaux risques climatiques et dont les impacts économiques et sociaux sont appelés à s’accentuer avec l’évolution du climat. Le changement climatique modifie les conditions auxquelles nos villes et nos territoires doivent désormais se préparer. L’Organisation météorologique mondiale souligne d’ailleurs la multiplication des épisodes météorologiques extrêmes et l’importance des systèmes d’alerte et d’adaptation. Nous ne pouvons donc plus penser l’assainissement avec les seules réalités climatiques du passé. Notre pays connaît lui aussi une vulnérabilité croissante face aux inondations, aussi bien dans les grandes agglomérations que dans les zones périurbaines et rurales. À Dakar, les épisodes récents ont particulièrement affecté plusieurs secteurs des Parcelles Assainies, Grand-Yoff, Front de Terre, Castors, Pikine, Diamaguène, Mbao, Guédiawaye, Keur Massar et Rufisque, avec des difficultés de circulation et des habitations ou infrastructures exposées. Mais le problème ne s’arrête pas à la capitale. Des territoires ruraux et d’autres régions du pays sont également confrontés aux conséquences des fortes précipitations, aux débordements, aux difficultés d’accès et aux dommages causés aux habitations, aux infrastructures et aux activités économiques. Les données nationales montrent que la récurrence des inondations touche depuis plusieurs années des populations importantes au Sénégal, avec une vulnérabilité particulièrement marquée dans les zones urbaines et périurbaines. Dakar, les autres villes et nos territoires ruraux doivent donc être pensés dans une même stratégie nationale de résilience. La pluie n’est pas notre ennemie. Elle fait partie de notre climat. Notre véritable défi est notre capacité à anticiper, canaliser, stocker, traiter, évacuer et valoriser l’eau. Dakar est une capitale particulière; une presqu’île, une métropole densément peuplée et le principal centre administratif, économique, commercial, sanitaire et éducatif du pays. Pourtant, quelques heures de fortes pluies peuvent suffire à perturber profondément son fonctionnement : routes impraticables, quartiers isolés, transports ralentis, travailleurs empêchés de rejoindre leur lieu de travail, activités commerciales perturbées, accès aux établissements de santé et aux écoles rendu difficile. Les fortes pluies du 4 octobre 2026 ont encore illustré cette vulnérabilité : la mobilité entre Dakar et sa banlieue a été fortement perturbée et plusieurs secteurs de Pikine, Diamaguène, Mbao, Guédiawaye et Keur Massar ont été affectés. L’assainissement ne doit donc plus être considéré comme une simple question technique. C’est un enjeu économique, social, environnemental et stratégique. Il ne suffit plus d’attendre les premières pluies pour mobiliser les motopompes et intervenir sur les points critiques. Ces interventions d’urgence sont nécessaires, mais elles doivent s’inscrire dans une politique permanente d’anticipation et de prévention. Je propose ainsi l’ouverture d’une réflexion nationale autour d’un objectif ambitieux :Dakar zéro inondation Une ambition progressive, mesurable et fondée sur l’expertise avec 10 axes stratégiques proposés: 1. Cartographier les zones à risques 2. Développer une surveillance intelligente des eaux 3. Moderniser et entretenir les réseaux 4. Développer les bassins de rétention et espaces de stockage 5. Faire de l’eau de pluie une ressource 6. Étudier les possibilités d’évacuation maîtrisée vers le littoral 7. Moderniser les réseaux d’eaux pluviales et d’eaux usées 8. Faire respecter les règles d’urbanisme. 9. Mettre en place un plan de résilience économique. 10. Faire de chaque commune un acteur de la prévention. Cette réflexion n’est dirigée contre aucune institution. Elle doit nous permettre de dépasser les polémiques et de construire des solutions qui dépassent les mandats politiques. Dakar appartient à ceux qui y vivent aujourd’hui, mais aussi à ceux qui y vivront demain. Nous devons donc penser au-delà de l’urgence et inscrire notre action dans une véritable vision de transformation urbaine et territoriale. Je rêve d’un Dakar où la pluie ne provoque plus la peur. Un Dakar où les routes restent accessibles, où les quartiers bénéficient d’infrastructures adaptées, où l’eau est récupérée et valorisée, où la technologie permet d’anticiper les risques et où l’environnement est protégé. Un Dakar propre, accessible, connecté, résilient et durable, à la hauteur du Sénégal que nous voulons construire. Les pluies de ces derniers jours doivent être plus qu’un épisode difficile. Elles doivent être un électrochoc. L’heure est à l’expertise. L’heure est à la planification. L’heure est à l’investissement. L’heure est à la responsabilité. L’assainissement de Dakar doit devenir un chantier majeur de la transformation de notre capitale, tout en inscrivant cette ambition dans une politique nationale de résilience face aux changements climatiques. Parce que Dakar ne doit plus être une ville qui attend la pluie pour chercher des solutions. Et notre ambition doit être claire : DAKAR ZÉRO INONDATION À L’HORIZON 2050 Pour protéger nos populations. Pour préserver notre économie. Pour créer des emplois. Pour protéger notre environnement. Pour préparer notre jeunesse. Et pour transmettre aux générations futures une capitale dont nous pouvons être fiers. Dakar doit devenir une solution, jamais un problème. Khouraichi Thiam Administrateur Générale du FAISE

items.title: Code pétrolier : le Conseil constitutionnel déclare irrecevable la proposition de débat préalable à l’Assemblée
items.description: Le Conseil constitutionnel a déclaré irrecevable, lundi 5 octobre 2026, la proposition de loi n°37/26 visant à modifier l’article 20 du Code pétrolier pour soumettre les contrats de partage de production à un débat préalable en séance plénière de l’Assemblée nationale. La haute juridiction estime que cette disposition relève du domaine réglementaire et non de celui de la loi. Saisi le 28 septembre 2026 par le Premier ministre Ahmadou Alhaminou M. Lo., le Conseil constitutionnel devait trancher un désaccord entre le Gouvernement et l’Assemblée nationale sur la nature juridique de la disposition introduite par la proposition de loi. Le recours demandait de déclarer que cette disposition avait un caractère réglementaire et, en conséquence, de constater l’irrecevabilité de l’ensemble du texte. Au cœur du texte contesté figurait une nouvelle étape dans la procédure d’approbation des contrats de partage de production. La proposition prévoyait que ces contrats soient approuvés par décret et publiés au Journal officiel après avoir été obligatoirement soumis par le président de la République à l’Assemblée nationale pour un débat en séance plénière, sans vote. Pour le Premier ministre, cette exigence ajoutait une formalité entre la signature du contrat et son approbation, alors que la procédure d’approbation relève du pouvoir réglementaire. Le Gouvernement estimait également que l'organisation d'un débat parlementaire préalable constituait une modalité d'exercice d'une compétence administrative et exécutive. Dans son mémoire en réponse, le président de l’Assemblée nationale, Ousmane Sonko, avait défendu une lecture différente. Il soutenait que le texte ne donnait aucun pouvoir d’approbation ou de rejet à l’Assemblée nationale et ne subordonnait pas l’approbation des contrats à un vote parlementaire. Selon lui, le débat prévu devait notamment renforcer la transparence, le contrôle et l’information de la représentation nationale sur l’utilisation des ressources naturelles. Une saisine préalable de l’Assemblée avant la signature du décret d’approbation Le Conseil constitutionnel a reconnu que les règles substantielles relatives à l’exploitation et à la gestion des ressources naturelles peuvent relever du domaine de la loi. Il a toutefois établi une distinction avec les dispositions qui déterminent les conditions d’exercice du pouvoir de signer les décrets, compétence directement attribuée au président de la République par l’article 43 de la Constitution. La haute juridiction relève que le débat parlementaire prévu ne confère effectivement aucun pouvoir de décision à l’Assemblée nationale, puisque celui-ci n’est pas suivi d’un vote. Elle considère néanmoins que la saisine préalable de l’Assemblée et la tenue de ce débat deviennent une condition que le président de la République doit remplir avant de pouvoir signer le décret d’approbation. Pour le Conseil constitutionnel, cette disposition ne se limite donc pas à organiser l’information ou le contrôle de l’action du Gouvernement. Elle fixe une condition procédurale à l’exercice du pouvoir réglementaire. Or, selon la décision, cette matière n’est réservée par aucune disposition constitutionnelle au domaine de la loi et présente, par conséquent, un caractère réglementaire au sens de l’article 76 de la Constitution. Le Conseil constitutionnel en déduit que la disposition en cause n’étant pas du domaine de la loi, elle est irrecevable en application de l’article 83 de la Constitution. La proposition de loi n°37/26 portant modification de l’article 20 de la loi n°2019-03 du 1er février 2019 portant Code pétrolier est ainsi déclarée irrecevable.

items.title: El Malick Ndiaye à Conakry : « Entre Sénégalais et Guinéens, nous sommes tellement voisins qu’il devient difficile de savoir où se trouve la famille »
items.description: À l’occasion de la rentrée de la 10ᵉ législature de la République de Guinée, le vice-président de l’Assemblée nationale du Sénégal, El Malick Ndiaye, grande figure du Pastef, principale formation politique au Sénégal, a livré ce lundi 5 octobre un message axé sur les liens historiques et fraternels entre les peuples sénégalais et guinéen. Représentant le président de l’Assemblée nationale du Sénégal, Ousmane Sonko, El Malick Ndiaye a insisté sur la proximité particulière entre les deux pays, appelant à renforcer davantage la coopération entre leurs institutions parlementaires. « Entre Sénégalais et Guinéens, nous sommes parfois tellement voisins qu’il devient difficile de savoir où se trouve la famille et où commence la démocratie », a-t-il déclaré. Pour le responsable sénégalais, cette proximité doit se traduire par une collaboration institutionnelle plus étroite. « Nos parlements ne doivent donc pas seulement se rencontrer lors de ces rencontres. Ils doivent travailler ensemble, apprendre les uns des autres », a-t-il souligné. El Malick Ndiaye a également plaidé pour une diplomatie parlementaire africaine davantage tournée vers le rapprochement des peuples et le renforcement des relations entre institutions. « Des voisins qui se respectent, des peuples qui restent frères et des institutions qui savent préserver ce qui les unit », a-t-il ajouté, estimant que c’est « tout le sens que nous devons donner à la diplomatie parlementaire africaine ». Sa présence à Conakry intervient dans le cadre de la rentrée de la 10ᵉ législature guinéenne, marquée par la participation de plusieurs délégations parlementaires africaines. items.title: At Oct 7 memorial, Netanyahu says will be no Hamas rule in Gaza
items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday vowed there would be no Hamas rule in Gaza as he attended a memorial event marking three years since the militant group’s October 7, 2023 attack. Monday is a national day of remembrance for the deadliest day in Israel’s history, with flags lowered to half-mast on public buildings from 6:29 am, the time the attack began. Speaking during a state ceremony at the Mount Herzl military cemetery in Jerusalem, Netanyahu said “we have achieved enormous accomplishments, but there are still missions ahead of us, and we intend to complete them”. “There will be no Hamas rule in Gaza,” he added, vowing to continue targeting anyone who was involved in the attack or who held hostages. In a separate speech later on Monday, Netanyahu said he stood with victims’ families and the nation shared their grief. “There is no forgiveness for the murderers, the torturers, the arsonists. There is no forgiveness for the destroyers, the looters, the kidnappers,” he said. Later in the speech, a heckler shouted: “You didn’t protect my son and 1,200 others killed on October 7 — shame!” leading Netanyahu to briefly pause the address. The Hamas-led attack resulted in the deaths of 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures. Militants also dragged 251 hostages into Gaza, 44 of them already dead. In response, Israel launched a massive military offensive that has killed more than 74,200 people in Gaza, according to the territory’s health ministry, which is under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations. Since a ceasefire was declared last October, Israeli forces have killed more than 1,440 people in Gaza, according to the ministry. Plans for Gaza’s post-war governance have begun to take shape, but the issue remains largely unresolved in practice. Since Hamas’s October 2023 attack, Israel has fought wars on several fronts, including against Iran-backed Hezbollah in Lebanon. During his speech on Monday, Netanyahu also vowed to keep striking Hezbollah to “create an opportunity for peace with a country whose people, for the most part, want peace with us”. Netanyahu also hit out at the clerical leadership in Iran, where Israel and the United States launched a joint attack on February 28, triggering the Middle East war. “We will not allow the ayatollah regime in Tehran to threaten our existence,” Netanyahu said, adding the Iranian leadership was “weaker than it has been since its establishment”. items.title: Rentrée scolaire à Matoto : une reprise effective, mais encore morose dans plusieurs établissements
items.description: La rentrée scolaire 2026-2027 a officiellement démarré ce lundi 5 octobre en Guinée. Mais dans plusieurs établissements visités dans la commune de Matoto, l’ambiance reste encore morose, avec une faible présence des élèves. Au Collège et Primaire Yaguine et Fodé, à l’école primaire Sangoyah Cité ainsi qu’au lycée Léopold Sédar Senghor, le constat est similaire : les élèves sont encore peu nombreux et la reprise des cours s’effectue progressivement. Présent sur le terrain pour constater le démarrage des cours, , Sékou Kaba, Directeur communal de l’Éducation (DCE) de Matoto , s’est réjoui de la reprise des activités scolaires. «C’est un sentiment de fierté, un sentiment de satisfaction pour la reprise des cours. Après trois mois de repos, les enseignants sont massivement présents », a déclaré le DCE de Matoto. Selon lui, les dispositions nécessaires avaient été prises pour accueillir les élèves dans de bonnes conditions. «L’école est assainie, propre. Les dispositions étaient déjà prises en amont avant le jour de cette rentrée scolaire », a-t-il précisé. Interrogé sur la faible affluence observée dans certaines écoles, Sékou Kaba estime que cette situation pourrait évoluer progressivement au cours des prochains jours:«Le premier jour de la rentrée, au niveau de certaines écoles, ce n’est pas tellement. Mais demain, ou après-demain, vous verrez que, au fur et à mesure, le nombre sera croissant », a-t-il expliqué. Le DCE de Matoto a également insisté sur la nécessité de privilégier la qualité de l’enseignement et l’assiduité des élèves:«Notre objectif principal, c’est une éducation performante. Qui parle d’éducation performante parle de la qualité », a-t-il souligné. À l’endroit des élèves, il a appelé au respect des règles scolaires et à une présence régulière en classe pour année scolaire réussie:«Chaque élève, en quittant la maison, ne doit pas prendre autre destination qu’à l’école. Et au retour, également la même chose.C’est aujourd’hui qu’il faut préparer la fin d’année. Parce qu’un élève qui refuse de chômer, un élève assidu, un élève qui arrive à repasser les cours une fois à la maison, cet élève ira très loin », a-t-il ajouté. Malgré la faible mobilisation constatée dans plusieurs établissements, certains élèves ont répondu présents. Au lycée Léopold Sédar Senghor, Hélène Kolomou, élève en Terminale, encourage ses amis à un retour scolaire : « Du fait que nous nous sommes retrouvés ici avec mes camarades de classe de la Terminale, ça m’a donné une belle joie.Je dirais aussi aux élèves qui ne sont pas d’abord présents ici de continuer l’école », a-t-elle lancé. Pour Hélène Kolomou, les premiers jours de cours constituent une étape importante :«Les premiers jours de l’école, c’est dans ce jour qu’on donne les programmes, et on donne aussi des conseils. Ces conseils venant du prof, ça nous encourage et ça nous motive à continuer l’école et à bien suivre les cours.» Ainsi, au terme de cette première journée, la rentrée est effective dans plusieurs établissements de Matoto, mais la mobilisation des élèves reste encore faible. Du Collège et Primaire Yaguine et Fodé à l’école primaire Sangoyah Cité, en passant par le lycée Léopold Sédar Senghor, le constat est celui d’une reprise progressive, avec l’espoir d’une affluence plus importante dans les prochains jours. items.title: Three missing children found dead in parked vehicle in Tamale
items.description: The Koblimahagu Zuo community in the Tamale Metropolis was thrown into mourning and shock on Monday morning following the discovery of three missing children who were found dead inside a parked vehicle. The deceased, aged, three, five and eight had reportedly been missing since Saturday, prompting a search for them and an appeal to the public for information on their whereabouts. The circumstances surrounding their disappearance and subsequent death is not yet known. Confirming the incident, the Assembly Member for the area, Seidu Fuseini, said the owner of the vehicle has been taken into custody by the police to assist with investigations. He said the vehicle owner told the police that he had locked all the doors of the vehicle before leaving it. A relative of one of the deceased children, Mohammed Juuna, in a social media post, said the children were found trapped inside a stationary vehicle within the community. They have since been conveyed to the morgue of the Tamale Teaching Hospital for autopsy. Police investigations are underway to help unravel the circumstances surrounding their disappearance and death.

items.title: Nana Akomea denies reports linking his absence from NPP executives’ introduction to Kojo Bamba
items.description: Newly elected New Patriotic Party (NPP) 3rd Vice Chairman Nana Akomea has denied reports suggesting that he and fellow newly elected executive Nana Bee were absent from the introduction of the party’s new national executives because they were upset over a failed arrangement involving Kojo Bamba. According to Mr Akomea, while he was indeed not present for the introduction, his absence had nothing to do with any disagreement or negotiation involving Mr Bamba or any other person. He explained that he had left the conference grounds at about 11:30 pm and was caught up in traffic while returning to the Kumasi stadium, arriving only a few minutes after the introductions had taken place. “I was not present during the vote counting and tabulation, and so could not have engaged myself in any ‘negotiation’ with Kojo Bamba or anybody else,” he said in a Facebook post on Monday, October 5. Mr Akomea’s clarification follows reports surrounding the absence of some newly elected executives during their introduction after the NPP’s national delegates congress in Kumasi.

items.title: Ondo crash: Aiyedatiwa mobilises rescue support
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure AKURE — Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, has expressed sympathy to the Chief of the Air Staff, the Nigerian Air Force and families of personnel and passengers aboard the aircraft that crashed in Igbokoda, Ilaje Local Government Area of the state. The governor also directed the State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), Ministry of Health and relevant security agencies to immediately mobilise logistical and human support for the ongoing search-and-rescue operation. The Nigerian Air Force confirmed that an ATR-42 aircraft on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos crashed in the Igbokoda area on Monday, October 5. Search-and-rescue operations are ongoing. In a statement issued by his Chief Press Secretary, Ebenezer Adeniyan, Aiyedatiwa said, “Our thoughts and prayers are with them at this difficult time.” According to the statement, the governor has been in contact with the leadership of the Nigerian Air Force, the Ilaje Local Government Chairman, Hon. Maurice Oripelaye, and security agencies on the ground. The statement read: “The Governor of Ondo State, His Excellency, Hon. Lucky Orimisan Aiyedatiwa, has received with deep sadness the news of the crash of a Nigerian Air Force aircraft in Igbokoda, headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, in the early hours of today, Monday, October 5, 2026. “According to preliminary reports confirmed by the Nigerian Air Force Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, the aircraft, an ATR-42 with tail number NGR 931, was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when it crashed in a swampy area opposite the Naval Base in Igbokoda. “The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr. Festus Keyamo, has confirmed that 25 passengers and seven crew members were on board. “On behalf of the Government and good people of Ondo State, Governor Aiyedatiwa expresses his heartfelt sympathy to the Chief of Air Staff, the entire Nigerian Air Force family, and the families of all personnel and passengers on board the ill-fated aircraft. Our thoughts and prayers are with them at this difficult time. “The Governor has been in contact with the leadership of the Nigerian Air Force, the Ilaje Local Government Chairman, Hon. Maurice Oripelaye, and security agencies on ground. “To aid ongoing efforts, Governor Aiyedatiwa has directed the State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), the Ministry of Health, and relevant security agencies to immediately mobilise and offer full logistical and human support to the Nigerian Air Force and other emergency response agencies in the search and rescue operations currently ongoing at the crash site. “The Governor has also directed that the area be cordoned off and secured to allow for smooth and unhindered rescue operations, while urging residents of Igbokoda and adjoining communities to remain calm, cooperate with emergency responders, and refrain from spreading unverified information. “The Ondo State Government will continue to monitor the situation and provide updates as more information becomes available from the Nigerian Air Force. “We pray for the safety of our gallant officers and for the success of the rescue efforts.” As of the latest official reports, authorities had not confirmed the condition of those aboard the aircraft. The post Ondo crash: Aiyedatiwa mobilises rescue support appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2026 U-17 WWC: Black Maidens arrive in Morocco for tournament
items.description: Ghana’s U-17 Women’s National Team have arrived in Morocco ahead of their return to the global stage after securing qualification. The Black Maidens touched down in Casablanca in the early hours of Monday, October 5, ahead of their participation in the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Nana Joe Adarkwa’s side take to the competition for the first time after suffering a two-edition ban from the Confederation of African Football (CAF). The team consists mainly of players who competed at the just-ended WAFU B Girls Cup in Cote d’Ivoire, as well as some of the players who played at the recent U-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland. Some notable players include Jessica Appiah Asamoah, who missed the U-20 World Cup due to an injury. Juliana Gyekyewaa, Priscilla Mensah and Latifa Musah all make the squad. Some of the players who also competed in the 2025 African School Championship with the Black Damsels have also been called up, including Christiana Ashiaku, Mavis Koah, Belinda Kpentey and Hajara Adams. Ghana is drawn in Group C, where they will face Norway, Brazil and Canada.

items.title: Disgraced former US House Speaker dies at 84
items.description: Dennis Hastert, the longest-serving Republican speaker of the US House of Representatives whose career ended in disgrace after he admitted sexually abusing teenage boys he had coached, has died aged 84, officials said Monday. The Kendall County Coroner’s Office in Illinois said Hastert died at his home Saturday night while under hospice care. Hastert was one of Washington’s most powerful politicians during eight years as House speaker from 1999 to 2007, a position that placed him second in the line of succession to the presidency. But his reputation collapsed years after he left Congress when a federal investigation into suspicious bank withdrawals exposed payments intended to conceal sexual abuse dating back to his years as a high school wrestling coach. Hastert pleaded guilty in 2015 to illegally structuring cash withdrawals to avoid bank reporting requirements as part of a $3.5 million agreement with one of his victims. At his sentencing the following year, Hastert admitted for the first time that he had sexually abused boys while teaching and coaching wrestling at Yorkville High School in Illinois from the 1960s to the early 1980s. “They looked to me and I took advantage of them,” Hastert said in court. Prosecutors detailed abuse involving at least five boys, some as young as 14. He could not be prosecuted for the sexual offenses because the statutes of limitations had expired, and was instead sentenced to 15 months in federal prison for violating banking laws. US District Judge Thomas Durkin described Hastert at sentencing as a “serial child molester.” Hastert served in the House from 1987 until 2007 and became speaker after the turbulent departure of fellow Republican Newt Gingrich and the withdrawal of Gingrich’s intended successor, Bob Livingston. He remained speaker until Democrats regained control of the House in the 2006 midterm elections. Hastert was released from federal prison in 2017 after serving most of his sentence. The post Disgraced former US House Speaker dies at 84 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: GPC contribue à la réalisation du Parc des Citoyens, nouvelle infrastructure urbaine et sportive au cœur de Conakry
items.description: Conakry, le 5 octobre 2026 – Le Groupe GPC, acteur guinéen de référence dans les domaines des infrastructures, de la logistique et des services miniers, a pris part à l’inauguration du Parc des Citoyens, après avoir contribué, à travers GPC Construction, à la réalisation de cette nouvelle infrastructure urbaine et sportive portée par le Gouvernement guinéen avec l’appui de Rio Tinto Simfer. La réalisation de la première phase du Parc a mobilisé les équipes de GPC autour d’un défi opérationnel important : livrer les travaux en 60 jours, dans un environnement climatique et technique exigeant. Au total, 420 834 heures de travail ont été réalisées sans accident avec arrêt, témoignant de l’attention portée à la sécurité tout au long du chantier. Cette première phase comprend notamment un terrain de football à 11, cinq terrains de basketball et trois terrains de tennis, ainsi qu’une piste d’athlétisme en tartan, une tribune de 1 000 places et 5 760 m² de parking, les voiries associées et la clôture du site. Les travaux ont été réalisés avec une main-d’œuvre composée à 97,28 % de Guinéens et 75 % de fournisseurs locaux, illustrant la capacité des compétences locales à contribuer à la réalisation d’infrastructures d’envergure. La dimension environnementale a également été intégrée au projet dès sa conception. Les aménagements comprennent 10 060 m² d’espaces verts, 30 000 plants et 245 lampes solaires. La proximité du Parc avec un bras de mer a par ailleurs nécessité la mise en œuvre de solutions de drainage adaptées, destinées à assurer la pérennité des infrastructures tout en préservant leur environnement. « La réalisation du Parc des Citoyens représente une grande fierté pour nos équipes. Au-delà de la performance technique, ce projet montre ce que nous pouvons accomplir lorsque nous associons expertise, compétences locales, sécurité et responsabilité environnementale. Je tiens à remercier le Gouvernement guinéen et Rio Tinto Simfer pour leur confiance, ainsi que toutes les équipes de GPC qui se sont mobilisées pour contribuer à donner vie à ce projet », a déclaré Amadou Kaba, CEO du Groupe GPC. Pensé comme un espace de vie accessible aux populations, le Parc des Citoyens offre désormais aux habitants de Conakry de nouveaux espaces dédiés au sport, aux loisirs, à la promenade et aux activités en famille. Environ 500 000 visiteurs par an sont attendus. La réalisation du Parc vient ainsi renforcer le portefeuille de références de GPC Construction dans les infrastructures urbaines et sportives et témoigne de la capacité du Groupe à mobiliser des compétences développées localement pour exécuter des projets complexes, avec une attention constante portée à la sécurité et à l’environnement. À propos de GPC Le Groupe GPC est un acteur guinéen de référence dans les domaines des infrastructures, de la logistique et des services miniers. Fortement ancré dans le tissu économique national, GPC met son expertise et son savoir-faire au service d’un développement durable, fiable et porté par les talents guinéens. Parc des Citoyens – 5 October 2026 version GPC contributes to the development of Parc des Citoyens, a new urban and sports infrastructure in the heart of Conakry Conakry, 5 October 2026 – GPC Group, a leading Guinean company in infrastructure, logistics and mining services, took part in the inauguration of Parc des Citoyens, having contributed, through GPC Construction, to the development of this new urban and sports infrastructure led by the Government of Guinea with the support of Rio Tinto Simfer. The delivery of the Park’s first phase mobilised GPC teams around a major operational challenge: completing the works within 60 days, in demanding climatic and technical conditions. In total, 420,834 working hours were completed without a lost-time accident, reflecting the strong focus placed on safety throughout the project. This first phase notably includes one 11-a-side football pitch, five basketball courts and three tennis courts, as well as a tartan athletics track, a 1,000-seat grandstand and 5,760 m² of parking, together with the associated roads and site fencing. The works were carried out with a workforce comprising 97.28% Guinean nationals and 75% local suppliers, illustrating the ability of local skills and expertise to contribute to the delivery of large-scale infrastructure. Environmental considerations were also integrated into the project from the design stage. The landscaping includes 10,060 m² of green spaces, 30,000 plants and 245 solar-powered lights. The Park’s proximity to an inlet also required the implementation of adapted drainage solutions designed to ensure the long-term durability of the infrastructure while preserving its surrounding environment. “The development of Parc des Citoyens is a great source of pride for our teams. Beyond the technical performance, this project demonstrates what we can achieve when we combine expertise, local skills, safety and environmental responsibility. I would like to thank the Government of Guinea and Rio Tinto Simfer for their trust, as well as all GPC teams who mobilised to help bring this project to life,” said Amadou Kaba, CEO of GPC Group. Designed as a public space accessible to communities, Parc des Citoyens now provides Conakry residents with new areas dedicated to sport, leisure, walking and family activities. Approximately 500,000 visitors are expected each year. The development of the Park further strengthens GPC Construction’s portfolio of references in urban and sports infrastructure and demonstrates the Group’s ability to mobilise locally developed expertise to execute complex projects, with a constant focus on safety and the environment.
