items.title: Aircraft crash: We can only investigate if invited by military – NSIB
items.description: By Dickson Omobola Following the crash of an ATR-42 aircraft in Igbokoda, Ondo State, the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) has offered to provide flight data and cockpit voice recovery and readout support to the Nigerian Air Force. NSIB, which said investigation of the accident rests with the military authority because it involved a military aircraft, added that its Flight Safety Laboratory could be deployed to assist with the recovery and analysis of flight data and cockpit voice recordings should the Nigerian Air Force formally request its assistance. A statement signed by NSIB Director General / Chief Executive Officer, Captain Alex Badeh Jr, reads: “NSIB has received reports of an accident involving a Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft in the Igbokoda area of Ondo State on 5 October 2026. The Nigerian Air Force has confirmed that the aircraft was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when the accident occurred and that search and rescue operations have been activated and are ongoing, in coordination with relevant authorities and emergency response agencies. “The Bureau extends its sincere condolences to the Nigerian Air Force and to the families and colleagues of all those on board. Our thoughts are with them and with the search and rescue teams working at the site. “This occurrence involves a military aircraft. In line with the NSIB Establishment Act, 2022, and with established international practice, the investigation of military aviation accidents rests with the military authority. The NSIB does not investigate military accidents unless formally invited to do so by that authority. “Should the Nigerian Air Force so request, the Bureau stands ready to assist. That assistance can include the deployment of investigators and the use of the Bureau’s Flight Safety Laboratory for flight data and cockpit voice recovery and readout, as well as related technical support. The NSIB commends the swift activation of search and rescue operations and the efforts of first responders at Igbokoda. The public is urged to rely exclusively on official updates from the Nigerian Air Force on the rescue operation and on any investigation.” The post Aircraft crash: We can only investigate if invited by military – NSIB appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Régions de Bankui et du Sourou : La Police nationale veille au respect strict du port obligatoire du casque en circulation
items.description: La Police nationale a mené des opérations de contrôle du port effectif du casque en circulation à l’échelle des régions de Bankui et du Sourou, du 1 er au 4 octobre 2026 . Les opérations de contrôle de l’effectivité du port du casque en circulation se mènent avec efficacité dans les régions de Bankui et du Sourou. Elles sont conduites par la Police nationale avec à sa tête le directeur régional, le commissaire divisionnaire de police Valentin Kaboré. Elles se sont intensifiées depuis le 1 er octobre 2026. Le directeur régional dit constater que beaucoup d’usagers se sont conformés à la mesure. Cependant, l’arbre ne doit pas cacher la forêt. Les agents de la Police nationale ont, entre le 1 er et le 4 octobre 2026, interpellé plus de 1 200 personnes pour non port du casque en circulation. Ces contrevenants à la mesure du port obligatoire du casque ont été verbalisés et soumis au payement de plus de 2 750 000 FCFA d’amendes forfaitaires au profit des caisses de l’État, à en croire Valentin Kaboré. Il a indiqué que le contrôle va se poursuivre avant d’inviter la population à se conformer à cette mesure en vigueur. Yacouba BELEM

items.title: Maîtrise des dépenses publiques : Le projet d’appui à la gouvernance et au développement du secteur privé lancé
items.description: Lomé, 5 oct. (ATOP) – Le ministère des Finances et du Budget a lancé, en collaboration avec la Banque africaine de développement (BAD) et l’Ecole nationale d’administration (ENA), une série de formations de renforcement des capacités des cadres de l’administration publique le lundi 5 octobre à Lomé. Cette initiative s’inscrit dans le Projet d’appui à la gouvernance et au développement du secteur privé (PAGDSP) financé par la BAD à hauteur de 9,22 milliards de FCFA. Ce projet vise à créer un environnement institutionnel propice à une croissance économique forte, durable et inclusive. Le cycle de formations a démarré avec un atelier destiné aux cadres de la Direction nationale du contrôle financier (DNCF) autour du thème « Contrôle de la solde et maîtrise de la masse salariale ». Il est le fruit de la convention de formations locales conclue entre le PAGDSP et l’ENA. Pendant un an, ce partenariat prévoit la réalisation de près de 40 sessions de formation au profit de 2 202 cadres et agents issus de 24 structures bénéficiaires sur toute l’étendue du territoire national. Cette première session permettra aux bénéficiaires d’assimiler les concepts fondamentaux du contrôle de la solde et de la masse salariale ; d’interpréter les données salariales de l’État pour identifier rapidement les anomalies et maîtriser les risques. Il leur permettra, également, de concevoir et d’implanter des systèmes de contrôle interne efficaces et modernes. Les participants seront capables de développer des tableaux de bord, des indicateurs de performance et des outils pratiques de suivi-évaluation des dépenses de personnel. Selon les organisateurs, cette formation constitue l’axe stratégique du contrôle de la solde et de maîtrise de la masse salariale. Pour eux, la maîtrise des dépenses du personnel reste un enjeu central pour la viabilité budgétaire et la soutenabilité des finances publiques au Togo. Cette première session cible 90 cadres de la DNCF. Ceux-ci seront formés en 3 sessions de 5 jours chacune, regroupant 30 participants par session en ce mois d’octobre. Le PAGDSP Le PAGDSP s’inscrit dans la continuité des interventions de la BAD au Togo (notamment après le PARCI 1 & 2, le PAMOCI, le PAGFI et le PAE-PND). Il a trois 3 composantes. La première traite de l’optimisation de la gestion des finances publiques et de la gouvernance financière. La deuxième composante aborde le renforcement du cadre institutionnel de promotion de l’investissement privé, et la troisième évoque la gestion du projet. Ce projet entend, surtout, renforcer la mobilisation des ressources financières internes et externes ; améliorer l’allocation des ressources, l’intégrité de la chaîne de dépense et la budgétisation sensible au genre. Il compte consolider la transparence et la lutte contre la corruption, et promouvoir et dynamiser le secteur privé. Le projet couvre l’administration et des acteurs de la gouvernance, notamment l’Office togolais des recettes (OTR), Initiative pour la transparence des industries extractives (ITIE), le Centre CENTIF, la HAPLUCIA, la Cour des comptes et l’Autorité de régulation de la commande publique (ARCOP). Dans le secteur privé et l’artisanat, le projet prend en compte l’Union des chambres régionales de métiers (UCRM), l’Agence nationale de promotion et de garantie de financement, et des Organisations de la société civile (OSC), entre autres. Le directeur national du contrôle financier, Akakpo Iyatan Komi, représentant le ministre des Finances et du Budget, a fait savoir que le programme a été conçu pour contribuer à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations togolaises. ATOP/KYA/DHK/BV

items.title: Reactions trail continued captivity of NYSC members
items.description: By Chidi Nkwopara OWERRI — Reactions have continued to trail the prolonged captivity of prospective members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) who were kidnapped in Imo State while travelling to orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. Chief Raymond Onuekwusi expressed concern over the continued captivity of the young people, saying their families were being subjected to severe emotional distress while the victims themselves could be facing serious difficulties in the hands of their abductors. He said: “While the families of the abducted youngsters are passing through serious and unimaginable pain, only God knows what the kidnap victims themselves are experiencing in the hands of their abductors. “Nobody can carelessly rule out psychological trauma, possible abuse and health challenges, as the victims remain in captivity. “Let us not forget that the only sin of the victims, which we can readily point at, is their willingness to serve their fatherland! I don’t know when this has become a crime. “However, this ugly incident has brought Imo State again into bad light. It is equally sad that the state government, to the best of my knowledge, is yet to issue any statement on the matter. “While there is nothing on ground in Imo State to show that such a catastrophic incident took place in the state on our Independence Day, it is most disturbing that our nation’s highways are unsafe. “Why can’t our governments protect human lives and property in this day and age? Is this not part of the oath our leaders took before going into office?” When reminded of a recent statement attributed to the state Commissioner of Police, Mr Audu Garba Bosso, that security agencies had identified the location where the abducted corps members were being held, Onuekwusi said the development would only be meaningful if it led to their safe rescue. “It may be a pleasing development but nothing will be better for us all than rescuing them alive,” he said. He, however, expressed concern that the disclosure about the location of the victims could compromise security operations. “My serious fear is that the Imo police boss goofed, by giving out more information than was necessary. From what he gave out, will the criminals not take commensurate action against a possible counter attack?” he asked. Responding to criticisms levelled against him by Imo journalists, the Police Public Relations Officer, PPRO, Mr Henry Okoye, said he took public feedback seriously. “I take all public feedback seriously. Sometimes, silence simply means I am listening, reflecting, and considering the best way to respond. Please do not mistake my silence for disregard,” Okoye said. Meanwhile, the State Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Dr Onwuasoanya FCC Jones, said the party and government were committed to securing the release of the abducted prospective corps members. He said: “The APC administration places great value on the life of every Nigerian and we will not allow non-state actors to threaten the lives of our citizens without serious and immediate response from the government. “The Commander-in-Chief, in collaboration with the Governor, has released every necessary resource and personnel to ensure that these citizens are safely rescued and the criminals made to face the full wrath of the law for attempting to harass ordinary Nigerians. “We urge Imolites of all political persuasions to join the APC in prayers for the successful rescue of these innocent citizens, while we also encourage citizens who reside around the communities where these criminals are hiding to be free to provide the security agents with information and communal support required to root out the bad eggs from their hideout and make our communities safe for law-abiding citizens and residents.” Reacting to the statement, a citizen, Chidi Okoroafor, criticised the APC’s response, describing it as “shoddy” and saying it failed to address what he considered a wider public reaction to the abduction. He said: “Beyond the shoddy writing, your statement also failed to address a more serious moral failure. “While fellow Nigerian citizens, including young corps members, were still being held captive by criminals, many people went ahead with Independence Day celebrations as if nothing was wrong. “Instead of a national mood of disappointment, concern and collective anxiety, we witnessed noise, dancing and festivity. That is not resilience; it is callous indifference.” The post Reactions trail continued captivity of NYSC members appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Rivers seals 21 health facilities, arrests three
items.description: Facilities linked to alleged baby trafficking, racketeering By Davies Iheamnachor PORT HARCOURT — The Rivers State Government has sealed 21 health facilities over alleged involvement in baby trafficking and other regulatory violations, with three persons arrested for prosecution. The crackdown, conducted across four local government areas by the Rivers State Ministry of Health in the third quarter of 2026, included a joint operation with the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP) at Manda Clinic and Maternity, Elelenwo. According to the ministry, a Liberian national reportedly disclosed during the operation that three children had been procured from the facility within one month. The Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Health, Dr Vincent Wachukwu, disclosed this on Monday during the ministry’s third-quarter press briefing in Port Harcourt. Wachukwu said the enforcement followed surveillance reports indicating that more than 150 health facilities were operating without registration and regulatory supervision. He said the 21 facilities sealed comprised eight hospitals, five maternity homes and eight diagnostic centres across Port Harcourt, Obio/Akpor, Ikwerre and Etche Local Government Areas. According to him, 19 of the facilities were found operating without registration and below the minimum standards set by the ministry, while another registered facility was found operating without a licensed doctor or nurse. He said: “The Rivers State Ministry of Health is fully committed to its regulatory function and is committed to eradicating quackery from Rivers State as part of our mandate on health security. “This exercise is a continuation of our anti-quackery mandate to stamp out all unregistered facilities and facilities operated without the minimum standards.” Wachukwu said Manda Clinic and Maternity, Elelenwo, in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area, was operating without registration and had no licensed medical practitioners. He added that its operators were arrested by NAPTIP following the joint operation, after which the facility was sealed by the ministry. Other facilities shut include Vasty Clinic, Omoku; Danny Clinic and Daba Clinic in Old Port Harcourt Town; Kambel Hospital, Abara-Etche; Havilla Hospital, Igwuruta; Golden Era Hospital, Igwuruta; and Ola-Oluwa Hospital, Igwuruta. Wachukwu said Havilla Hospital was an unregistered facility operated by a man identified as Mr Isaac, who claimed to have undergone medical training in Ukraine in 2013 but had no licence from the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN). He added that Kambel Hospital, Abara-Etche, and Golden Era Hospital, Igwuruta, were shut after inspectors found that neither a licensed doctor nor nurse was operating the facilities. On Sarah Maternity, Belema Polo, Enugu Waterside, the Permanent Secretary said the facility, operated by a popular social media traditional birth attendant, had a patient load of more than 1,000 women and daily traffic of over 200 women. He said the ministry used the inspection to establish practice guidelines, supervision and advertisement standards, while the operator was issued an official warning and designated as a contact point for other traditional birth attendants and maternity operators on the need for supervision and training. Wachukwu said the remaining 16 facilities sealed during the exercise were found to be unregistered and operating below the minimum standards stipulated under the Rivers State Facility Registration Act No. 2 of 2019. He warned that the ministry would sustain the enforcement campaign and urged residents to patronise only health facilities that meet the state’s regulatory requirements. He said: “We mandate all registered facilities to display their Certificate of Standards at the reception of their facilities. “We also mandate individuals and corporate organisations to only access care in facilities with verified Certificates of Standards, as this serves as the quality assurance check for health security.” The post Rivers seals 21 health facilities, arrests three appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Plateau govt condemns attack on Jos South traders
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The Plateau State Government has condemned the attack on traders returning from the Bukuru Kara Livestock Market in Jos South Local Government Area of the state, describing the incident as sad and unacceptable. The government, in a statement signed on Monday by the Commissioner for Information and Communication, Joyce Lohya Ramnap, said security agencies had been directed to investigate the circumstances surrounding the attack, including the identities and motives of those responsible. It said the directive was aimed at further protecting lives and property within the Jos-Bukuru metropolis, while extending condolences to the victims and their families. “The Government, under the leadership of Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang, extends condolences to the families and victims of the incident,” the statement said. “To further protect lives and property within the Jos-Bukuru metropolis, the Plateau State Government has directed security agencies to investigate the circumstances surrounding the attack, including the identities and motives of those responsible,” it added. The government called on communities, traders, pastoralists and other stakeholders to remain calm and resist attempts to escalate tensions or deepen divisions. “There must be no room for reprisal attacks or the taking of the law into individual hands,” it warned. “While security agencies continue their investigation, the Government is engaging relevant stakeholders to strengthen security along vulnerable routes and prevent further attacks,” the statement said. It urged citizens to provide useful information to security authorities that could assist the investigation. The government reaffirmed that it “remains committed to protecting lives and property and building a peaceful environment where all law-abiding citizens can live, work and pursue their legitimate businesses without fear.” It therefore urged citizens to remain calm and go about their lawful activities. The post Plateau govt condemns attack on Jos South traders appeared first on Vanguard News .

France-Bénin : Romuald Wadagni reçu à l’Élysée par Emmanuel Macron
items.description: Le président béninois, Romuald Wadagni, a été reçu ce lundi 5 octobre 2026 au Palais de l’Élysée par son homologue français, Emmanuel Macron, dans le cadre de sa première visite de travail en France depuis son accession à la magistrature suprême. Au cours de cette rencontre, selon la présidence de la république du Bénin, les deux chefs d’État ont eu un entretien en tête-à-tête, suivi d’une réunion bilatérale consacrée aux principaux dossiers d’intérêt commun entre Cotonou et Paris. Plusieurs accords de coopération et de financement doivent également être signés à l’occasion de cette visite. Parmi les secteurs concernés figurent notamment l’électricité, l’agriculture, la pisciculture et la santé. Un programme de développement et d’extension des réseaux électriques est notamment associé à un financement annoncé de 173 millions d’euros. Un autre accord porte sur le développement de la filière piscicole et les investissements agricoles productifs, tandis qu’un partenariat prévoit la mise en place au Bénin d’un laboratoire d’excellence en hématologie médico-légale, avec un volet consacré au transfert de compétences. Cette visite constitue la première venue officielle de Romuald Wadagni en France depuis son investiture. Elle intervient dans le cadre d’une séquence diplomatique destinée à renforcer le dialogue entre Cotonou et Paris et à approfondir leur coopération dans plusieurs domaines prioritaires. La rencontre intervient également après la participation du chef de l’État béninois au dîner de l’Africa-France Impact Coalition (AFIC), organisé dimanche 4 octobre à l’Élysée. Cette rencontre avait réuni des dirigeants et acteurs économiques autour des questions d’investissement, d’innovation et de développement du continent africain. Minute.bf

items.title: INEC to track illegal campaign spending, vows sanctions for violence, vote-buying
items.description: ABUJA — The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has said it will track illegal campaign spending and sanction political parties, candidates and agents involved in violence, hate speech and vote-buying ahead of the 2027 general election. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the warning on Monday in Abuja at a strategic workshop for editors organised by the Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) in collaboration with the commission. Amupitan said the commission was working with relevant government agencies to monitor campaign finances and curb the influence of money on the electoral process. He said the commission was collaborating with the Federal Ministry of Justice, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU). “Joint financial monitoring teams will be deployed to track illegal campaign spending and conduct undercover surveillance at polling units nationwide,” Amupitan said. He warned political actors and their agents against attempting to buy votes with cash or material inducements, saying offenders would be arrested and prosecuted under the Electoral Act 2026. “Attempt to trade cash or material gifts for votes, and you will face immediate arrest and prosecution under the Electoral Act 2026,” he said. The INEC chairman also warned against political violence, intimidation and inflammatory rhetoric as parties intensify their campaigns ahead of the election. “As electioneering intensifies across the country, I must sound a clear note of warning to all political parties, candidates and campaign managers: INEC will not stand by and allow political competition to devolve into violence, intimidation or inflammatory rhetoric,” he said. According to him, the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) has activated an early-warning framework to monitor political violence, thuggery and dangerous campaign rhetoric. Amupitan said parties and candidates found inciting violence, disrupting opponents’ rallies or deploying armed thugs would face sanctions and prosecution. “No political office in this country is worth the blood of a single Nigerian,” he said. He also expressed concern over the alleged use of firearms in political campaigns, citing an incident he said had been brought to his attention shortly before his address. He urged politicians and citizens to act responsibly, stressing that elections were a periodic process for choosing leaders and should not become a source of violence. The post INEC to track illegal campaign spending, vows sanctions for violence, vote-buying appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Un homme interpellé pour des faits de pédophilie
items.description: Le Poste de Police de Médina Fall à Thiès au Sénégal a interpellé un homme pour des faits de pédophilie, selon un écrit de l’institution policière sur sa page Facebook, ce lundi 5 octobre 2026. Suspecté de pédophilie et d’attouchements sexuels, un homme a été mis aux arrêts à Thiès. L’enquête qui a permis son arrestation, «a été ouverte suite à une plainte déposée le 1er octobre 2026 par la mère de la victime», écrit la police sénégalaise. «Séparée du père de sa fille, la plaignante avait confié cette dernière pour un séjour à Tivaouane. C'est lors d'un échange sur ses conditions de vie au domicile paternel à Thiès que l'enfant s'est confiée à sa mère, révélant subir des abus sexuels répétés de la part du mis en cause, qui n'est autre que le chambellan de son père résidant dans la même maison», rapporte la police. La police affirme avoir auditionné la mineure en présence de sa mère, et elle a «livré un récit circonstancié corroborant les accusations», soulignant que «face à la gravité des faits, les enquêteurs ont immédiatement interpellé le suspect». «Lors de son audition, le mis en cause est passé aux aveux complets, allant jusqu'à reconnaître que ces agissements criminels duraient depuis 2021 à l'insu de l'entourage», dit la police qui déclare que «le mis en cause a été placé en garde à vue et l'enquête suit son cours». Par Wakat Séra L’article Un homme interpellé pour des faits de pédophilie est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Asagba Azinge: Peace drives Asaba’s development
items.description: Oborevwori, Okowa, monarchs hail two-year reign By Egufe Yafugborhi & Ochuko Akuopha ASABA — The Asagba of Asaba, His Royal Majesty Professor Epiphany Azinge, has attributed the development recorded in Asaba over the past two years to peace, describing it as the foundation upon which progress in the kingdom has been built. Azinge spoke on Monday in Asaba while marking the second anniversary of his coronation, as Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta State, former Governor Ifeanyi Okowa, traditional rulers and other stakeholders commended his leadership, peace-building efforts and developmental initiatives. Reflecting on his two years on the throne, Azinge said the responsibilities of traditional leadership were demanding, noting that each day on the throne came with significant challenges. “Let me make this public confession, that a day on the throne is like a lifetime. One can then easily come to terms with that saying that ‘uneasy lies the head that wears the crown,’” he said. The monarch said the anniversary was not primarily about celebrating his achievements but about recognising the importance of peace to the development of Asaba. “Firstly, to underscore the fact that it means so much for peace to reign in a kingdom, and that we’ve had peace in this kingdom in the last two years means so much to me. “Peace is the industry that we harness, and with peace comes all forms of development. So we will not be recounting our developmental trajectory today if there had been no peace in this kingdom,” Azinge said. He thanked residents and other stakeholders for their contributions to maintaining peace in the kingdom, saying the progress recorded was a collective achievement. “I want to applaud and I thank all that have made this possible for peace to reign,” he said. Azinge also commended the people of Asaba for their support, stressing that his vision for the kingdom could not be achieved without their cooperation. “I may dream the dreams, possibly see visions, but nothing can work out, nothing can thrive, nothing can flourish without the support of Asaba people,” he said. The monarch said his reign had also focused on strengthening relationships with traditional rulers across Delta State and beyond as part of efforts to promote unity and peaceful coexistence. “I’ve been able to engage with them one after the other, and together we’ve been able to chart a path for the future of our state,” he said. Azinge reaffirmed his support for the Delta State Government, describing the people of Asaba as partners in progress with the administration. “We have seen ourselves and the people of Asaba as partners in progress in whatever is going on in this state,” he said. Representing Governor Oborevwori at the event, the Chief of Staff, Hon. Johnson Erijo, commended Azinge for his commitment to peace, security and harmonious coexistence in Asaba. Erijo said the monarch had, in two years, “carried the responsibilities of this sacred stool with dignity, wisdom, and humility,” while promoting “peace, unity, and understanding among the people.” Former Governor Okowa also commended the monarch, saying Azinge’s reign had demonstrated that traditional leadership could contribute significantly to community development. “In just two years, there’s been a lot of transformation,” Okowa said, adding that Azinge was “rewriting traditional governance the way we thought it was in the past.” He particularly praised the monarch’s peace-building efforts, saying: “There is peace in Asaba. But beyond Asaba, you’ve been connecting with your fellow traditional rulers in so much humility.” The Chairman of the Delta State Council of Traditional Rulers, represented by Obi Henry A. Kikachukwu, also commended Azinge, saying, “Within two years, we have witnessed remarkable developments.” Azinge, however, attributed the progress to divine grace and the support of the people. “Whatever we may have achieved, I will always say it’s not by my might. It’s by the special grace of God,” he said. He added: “I will remain very humble, I will continue to make sacrifices on behalf of my people because I’m here to serve you.” Also present was His Majesty Igwe Chidubem Iweka, Eze Iweka III of Obosi Kingdom and Chairman of the Anambra State Council of Traditional Rulers. Iweka III offered prayers for Azinge, saying: “May those who don’t agree that you’ll be sitting on that throne, may they eventually agree more than those who agreed before. It shall be well with you.” The post Asagba Azinge: Peace drives Asaba’s development appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: FG commissions 10 diagnostic, three cancer centres — Pate
items.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Federal Government has completed 10 radiodiagnostic centres and three cancer centres across Nigeria as part of efforts to transform the country’s healthcare system, the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, has said. Pate disclosed this in Bauchi while speaking during the commissioning of a radiodiagnostic centre at the Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital (ATBUTH), Bauchi. He said the 10 diagnostic centres were executed through MedSafe and the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority (NSIA), describing the development as the largest expansion of health infrastructure and equipment in Nigeria’s history. According to him, the foundation for the Bauchi diagnostic centre was laid about two years ago, and the facility has now been completed alongside nine others located in different parts of the country. “This marks the largest expansion of health infrastructure and equipment in Nigeria’s history,” Pate said. He explained that the facilities were designed to provide Nigerians with access to modern diagnostic services and quality healthcare, while also supporting training and research. Pate said the commissioning of the Bauchi facility would be followed by the commissioning of another centre in Ibadan, Oyo State, while the remaining eight diagnostic centres had already been completed across the country. He described the projects as a major step in President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration’s efforts to revamp the health sector through the provision of modern diagnostic equipment, infrastructure and improved hospital services. The minister also disclosed that the Federal Government had completed three cancer centres as part of the broader healthcare transformation programme. He commended the collaboration between the Federal Government and state governments, stressing that such partnerships were essential to expanding access to quality healthcare services across the country. Pate further announced that preparations were underway for the establishment of six major multi-specialty hospitals, with one to be located in each of Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones. He said the planned hospitals would further expand the country’s healthcare infrastructure and access to specialised medical services. The minister thanked the Bauchi State Government for its cooperation and support, saying the Federal Government remained committed to working with subnational governments to improve healthcare delivery and the wellbeing of Nigerians. The post FG commissions 10 diagnostic, three cancer centres — Pate appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tchaoudjo : La FESAM encourage les meilleures élèves filles de l’EPP Abatchang
items.description: Sokodé, 5 oct. (ATOP) – Les cinq meilleures élèves filles de chaque classe de l’Ecole primaire publique (EPP) Abatchang, dans le canton de Lama-Téssi, (commune Tchaoudjo 2), ont bénéficié, le samedi 3 octobre dans leur établissement, de kits scolaires. Cette initiative est l’œuvre de l’association Femmes solidaires pour un avenir meilleur (FESAM). Les kits sont composés de cahiers, stylos, ardoise, règle, couvertures kaki et d’ensemble géométrique. Ce geste vise à encourager l’excellence scolaire et à motiver les élèves de sexe féminin à redoubler d’efforts dans leurs études. Des boîtes de craies ont, également, été offertes aux enseignants afin de contribuer à l’amélioration des conditions d’enseignement et d’apprentissage. Mme Edéou remettant le kit à une bénéficiaire L’association a, par ailleurs, apporté des sacs de vêtements pour tout âge à la population. La cérémonie a été marquée par la remise symbolique des kits aux bénéficiaires, en présence des responsables de l’établissement, des enseignants, des parents et des membres de l’association. La présidente de la FESAM, Mme Edéou Yowoudèma a confié que cette action matérialise l’engagement de l’association à accompagner les efforts du gouvernement pour l’épanouissement des jeunes filles et femmes en milieu rural. Elle a fait savoir que la FESAM œuvre aussi pour une meilleure scolarisation de la jeune fille et apporte son aide aux femmes rurales pour mener à bien leurs activités génératrices de revenus. « Notre intervention consiste à soutenir également, les acteurs de l’éducation avec l’espoir de contribuer à la construction d’un avenir meilleur pour les enfants », a-t-elle conclu. Le directeur de l’EPP Abatchang, Sakiè Kossi et le président du bureau des parents d’élèves, Sama Elouwa ont exprimé leur reconnaissance aux donateurs et se sont engagés à faire bon usage des fournitures reçues. Pour eux, ce geste constitue un appui important qui vient renforcer les efforts déployés quotidiennement pour assurer une éducation de qualité aux apprenants. L’association FE.S.AM est créée en 2016 à Lomé. Elle intervient dans les domaines social, économique, de l’éduction et de la santé. ATOP/BTP/MEK/HKM

items.title: Elevate Africa confirms presidents, vice presidents and ministers for 2026 Annual Convening in Accra
items.description: Elevate Africa has confirmed a high-level lineup of presidents, vice presidents, ministers, parliamentarians and continental policymakers for its 2026 Annual Convening, taking place on 28 and 29 October 2026 at the Mövenpick Ambassador Hotel in Accra, Ghana. T be held under the theme “Africa: Defining Her Future”, the convening will bring together leaders and influential voices from across Africa and the diaspora to discuss the continent’s economic and social future, with a focus on trade, governance, investment, culture and the creative economy. Among the confirmed government leaders are Dr Julius Maada Bio, President of the Republic of Sierra Leone and Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang, Vice President of the Republic of Ghana. They will be joined by former heads of state Dr Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, former President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria; Dr Joyce Banda, former President of the Republic of Malawi; Dr. Ameenah Gurib, former President of Mauritius and John Kufuor, former President of Ghana. Ministers confirmed to attend include Abla Dzifa Gomashie, Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts of Ghana; Barr. Hannatu Musa Musawa, Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy of Nigeria; and Ahmed Rostom, Minister of Planning of the Arab Republic of Egypt. Martha Karua, former Minister for Justice, National Cohesion and Constitutional Affairs of Kenya, will also participate. The senior representatives of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat will also take part, including Rui Livramento, Chief of Staff; Dr Tei Kitcher, Senior Trade Economist; and Constance Besse-Moser, Senior Advisor to the Secretary-General. Their participation will contribute to discussions on continental integration, trade and the implementation of Africa’s economic agenda. Speaking ahead of the convening, Her Royal Majesty Olorì Atuwatsé III, Co-Founder of Elevate Africa, said, “Africa’s future will be defined by leaders who are willing to build across borders, collaborate beyond sectors and generations, and create space for the exchange of knowledge, experience and new ideas between them. This convening is designed to bring those voices into one room to discuss the continent’s challenges and to shape pathways for shared prosperity.” Over 400-600 delegates from across Africa and the diaspora are expected to attend. Discussions will centre on four interconnected pillars: Leadership and Governance; Trade, Investment and Doing Business in Africa; Youth Opportunity and Leadership; and the Diaspora, Return, Creative Economy and Soft Power. The sessions will explore AfCFTA implementation, regional investment, creative industries, leadership and governance, youth participation and the role of the diaspora in Africa’s economic transformation. Additional heads of state, senior ministers and government dignitaries are in the final stages of confirmation, with further speaker announcements expected ahead of the convening.

Con desventaja en el marcador, 7-5 y 5-3 en su contra, el ruso (30 años) no logró alcanzar una pelota y al golpearla a continuación (aparentemente con la intención de que rebotara en el muro) la envió directamente al aficionado. La bola impacto en el ojo derecho de este y tuvo que retirarse de las gradas. De inmediato, el juez Mohamed Lahyani anunció la eliminación directa del jugador de Moscú, siguiendo las directrices que marcan la normativa. Seguir leyendo

items.title: JEPPC 2026 : Les ministres chargés de la Justice et de l’Administration territoriale président la montée des couleurs en dioula
items.description: Dans le cadre de la 2e phase de la 3e édition des Journées nationales d'engagement patriotique et de participation citoyenne, les ministres chargés de la Justice et de l'Administration territoriale ont conjointement présidé une cérémonie de montée des couleurs en langue dioula, ce 5 octobre 2026. À cette occasion, le ministre d'État chargé de l'Administration territoriale a livré le message du Président du Faso. Sous le thème général « Produisons burkinabè, consommons burkinabè » , le mot d'ordre de cette deuxième phase est sans équivoque : « Tous pour le Made in Burkina : faisons de chaque achat un acte de souveraineté » . Le Président du Faso y rappelle que la nation se construit dans les champs, les ateliers, les boutiques et sur les tables des Burkinabè. « Celui qui vous nourrit finit par vous dicter sa volonté » , prévient-il dans son message. Trois verrous à faire sauter Le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré identifie trois obstacles qui maintiennent encore la dépendance économique du Burkina Faso. Le premier est la production. Malgré un potentiel avéré, l'eau dort dans les barrages, la mécanisation reste insuffisante et l'insécurité a éloigné des familles de leurs terres. Pourtant, les résultats obtenus prouvent que le pays peut se nourrir lui-même, avec plus de sept millions de tonnes de céréales produites et le cap du million de tonnes de riz franchi. Le deuxième verrou est la transformation. « Le coton ne doit plus quitter notre pays en balles pour nous revenir en chemises. Le karité ne doit plus partir en amandes pour nous revenir, après transformation ailleurs, en pommades, en crèmes ou en chocolat vendus à prix d'or » , indique le texte. Le troisième verrou est dans les mentalités. Le riz local cherche preneur pendant que le riz importé inonde les marchés. Le Faso Dan Fani est jugé cher quand la chemise importée passe pour normale. « Ce conditionnement doit être brisé. Servir ce que notre terre a produit n'est pas un signe de pauvreté. C'est un acte de fierté, un geste d'honneur, une affirmation de souveraineté » , lit-on dans le message. Des appels ciblés à chaque acteur Le Président du Faso s'adresse directement à chaque catégorie d'acteurs. Aux paysans, il rappelle qu'ils sont les premiers combattants de la souveraineté nationale. Aux femmes, productrices, transformatrices et gardiennes des cuisines, il reprend une formule de Thomas Sankara : « Si les femmes sont décidées à boycotter les produits importés, alors c'est la garantie. En libérant le génie créateur de nos femmes, nous libérons notre économie » Aux forestiers, il rappelle que reboiser est produire. Aux commerçants et artisans, le Président du Faso pose un choix net : « Être le relais de la production nationale ou l'auxiliaire de la dépendance étrangère. Choisissez votre camp » . Le message décline également des gestes concrets à adopter au quotidien. Au marché, demander l'origine avant le prix. À la maison, servir au moins un repas entièrement burkinabè chaque jour. Aux cérémonies, privilégier les mets, les boissons et les tenues du pays. Dans l'administration, faire de la préférence nationale une obligation de service public dans les cantines, les achats de fournitures et les marchés publics. Des ennemis nommés sans détour Le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré ne s'arrête pas aux appels positifs. Il désigne clairement les pratiques qui sabotent la souveraineté économique : la fraude, la contrebande, la spéculation sur les prix des vivres, la rétention de stocks, la diffusion de rumeurs sur la qualité des productions locales et les faux producteurs de « Made in Burkina ». Il pointe également ce qu'il appelle le boycott silencieux. « Ceux qui applaudissent le consommer national en public et remplissent leur table de produits importés en privé. À ceux-là, je le dis clairement : vous trahissez le combat que vous prétendez servir » , lit-on dans le texte. Le message s'achève sur une dimension panafricaine, citant Thomas Sankara devant les chefs d'État africains en 1987 : « Produisons ce dont nous avons besoin et consommons ce que nous produisons au lieu de l'importer » Trente-neuf ans après, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré reprend ce fil et l'étend à l'espace de la Confédération des États du Sahel, appelant à ouvrir davantage les marchés entre pays frères. Ce message, livré dans les institutions publiques à travers tout le pays, sonne comme une feuille de route économique autant que comme un test de cohérence pour chaque acteur public et privé du Burkina Faso. Josué TIENDREBEOGO Faso7 L’article JEPPC 2026 : Les ministres chargés de la Justice et de l'Administration territoriale président la montée des couleurs en dioula est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Violence: Call politicians to order, INEC Chair begs traditional rulers
items.description: …As Secretary bags Minna emirate’s title By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, has appealed to traditional rulers to intervene and restrain politicians from engaging in violence, hostility and mudslinging as campaigns build up for the 2027 general elections. Speaking in Minna, Niger State, during the turbanning of INEC’s Secretary, Rose Oriaran-Anthony, as the Gimbiyan Raya Kasan Minna at the Emir’s Palace, Amupitan urged political actors to focus strictly on issue-based campaigns. “Voting is a fundamental right under our Constitution, not a privilege. We appeal to our royal fathers to help us counsel politicians to conduct their campaigns peacefully and avoid campaigns of calumny. Campaigns should be based on issues and not heat up the system or breach law and order”, Amupitan counselled. He charged traditional institutions to leverage their moral authority to preserve public order throughout the electoral cycle, while also commending the Minna Emirate for recognizing and elevating women in leadership. In her response, Oriaran-Anthony expressed gratitude to the Emir of Minna for the honour, describing the title as a call to higher service aimed at driving community development, youth empowerment, and advocacy for gender equality. She urged parents nationwide to afford equal opportunities to all children regardless of gender, noting that any child can bring honour and progress to their family and nation. items.title: PTI long march: After Karak address, KP CM's convoy departs for Kohat
items.description: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday resumed PTI’s march as he addressed supporters in Karak, from where his convoy will depart for Kohat. The opposition has gone ahead with its march despite warnings from the Centre, which has vowed to prevent any gatherings in Islamabad. The protest aims to demand the release of jailed party founder and former prime minister Imran Khan. PTI decided to embark on the march after weekend talks with the federal government to bridge their differences failed for multiple reasons , particularly over the counterterrorism policy. As per an update by PTI after 6pm on Monday, the Afridi-led march was advancing from Karak towards Kohat. Addressing party supporters at Karak’s Jail Chowk in the afternoon, the chief minister again railed against the Centre’s counterterrorism policy and criticised past military operations and drone attacks. Afridi also referred to Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s remarks from a day earlier, wherein the latter called him “immature”. He went on to recall Punjab CM Maryam Nawaz’s remarks on the terrorism threat to her province, adding: “Suppose, I say that [my province] does not have a threat from India, but from the other three provinces, will you consider me mature?” The KP CM said, “If you deem it immature to speak about one’s province and people, then I have shown this immaturity yesterday, still do and will keep doing so.” Afridi contended that “wrong policies drafted behind closed doors were impacting all institutions”. Expressing his patriotism for Pakistan, the PTI leader said, “We also chant Pakistan zindabad , we stand up for the national anthem as well.” But he added that future generations might not do so as there were attempts to “divide Pakistan and spread hatred”. Insisting that his party was democratically presenting the public’s demands, Afridi warned that if the situation crossed all limits, neither would he be able to control the public “nor will anyone’s father have the courage” to do so. He asserted that only those policies would be implemented that the people and the youth desire, and which were in the interests of the nation. “We will not accept any decision taken behind closed doors that is against us, our province or Pakistan,” the KP CM added. He argued that Imran could secure his release if he wanted but was choosing to remain behind bars for the nation’s “freedom”. “He is free even in jail, and we are slaves even when free,” he quipped. The chief minister urged people to reach Swabi, adding that no one could even imagine or think of the next plan of action. Earlier, Afridi’s focal person for digital media Yar Muhammad Khan Niazi shared a video on X of PTI supporters welcoming the KP CM at Karak’s Jail Chowk. According to a post by CM Afridi, the people of Karak were to join the convoy at 12pm, with the departure set for 12:30pm, which faced a delay. The convoy plans to stay overnight in Kohat, and then resume the journey towards Peshawar at noon on Oct 6. It will spend the night near Mattani. On the afternoon of Oct 7, the caravan will depart from Budh Bair in Peshawar and spend the night near Charsadda Interchange. The protesters will then move forward the next afternoon and spend the night of Oct 8 at Khairabad. Notably, the KP CM has refrained from detailing the final leg of the trip to the federal capital and said the plan for the next phase would be announced at Khairabad. This screengrab from Google Maps shows the planned route of the PTI convoy from Lakki Marwat to Khairabad, where it is scheduled to reach on Oct 8. The march so far After launching the already-postponed march from Lakki Marwat on Sunday afternoon, the KP CM’s caravan reached Karak at night, where Afridi addressed supporters at Jail Chowk. Ahead of the march, movement on several roads in KP’s Dera Ismail Khan, Upper and Lower South Waziristan, Tank and Hangu was restricted under Section 144 for varying periods . On Monday, former KP CM Ali Amin Gandapur, who was leading PTI workers from DI Khan to Lakki Marwat, took a U-turn from Yarik because of road blockades and the prevailing law and order situation. Noting that Section 144 had been imposed in the area for three days, Gandapur stressed that the party leadership had clearly directed workers not to damage public property or engage in any activity that could worsen the situation. Nevertheless, he contended that the return should not be viewed as a withdrawal from the protest movement, but as a temporary decision. In Karachi , a planned protest campaign in different areas was disrupted after police deployed personnel at several locations, blocked roads and detained several party workers and leaders. The PTI claimed that police detained more than 75 of its leaders and workers, including women, from different parts of Karachi. It further alleged that arrests made in other parts of Sindh, including Sukkur, put the total number of detained PTI workers across the province at more than 100. On Saturday night, an opposition delegation comprising PTI and Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), and a joint team of the government and PPP held hours-long negotiations , which ended in a deadlock. While the federal government blamed CM Afridi for the failure of negotiations, PTI denied the allegations and claimed that access to Imran, his medical treatment and the federal government’s counterterrorism policy were the key reasons. According to PTI, the government agreed to restore meetings between Imran and his family members and lawyers from Tuesday, but “declined to make access to Imran Khan part of the proposed agreement”.

items.title: Keta MP commissions 60-seater kindergarten facility to replace unsafe structure
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Keta Constituency, Dzudzorli Kwame Gakpey, has commissioned a 60-seater kindergarten classroom facility at the Anlo State School. The new facility replaces an old structure that had developed cracks, posing a danger to pupils. Detailing the project specifications to JoyNews, Director of Hab -Amenyo Co. Ltd., Amanyo Kwame Kattey, said the facility has two 30-seater classrooms, modern washrooms, storerooms and a headteacher’s office. “It is a complete classroom which we completed even before schedule. I was given eight months to build this, but I completed it within three months,” he added. Speaking at the commissioning ceremony, MP Dzudzorli Gakpey said he is liaising with the Ministry of Education to recruit more teachers into the municipality to address the teacher shortage and students’ poor performance. “The performance of students this year has not been the best across the country, but I am not happy with the grades of our children at all. Our children are not learning. We all need to do more to improve on the performance.” “One major problem is the shortage of teachers in the Constituency. I have spoken to the Education Minister to send us more teachers. So, very soon, more teachers will be coming to add to the numbers,” Mr Gakpey assured. The 60-capacity KG classroom is one of two new school projects being commissioned on Monday, October 5. The other facility will also be commissioned later in the day at Atiavi, in the Keta Municipality. The project cost GHS 748,000.

items.title: « Tous pour le Made in Burkina » : Le message du Président du Faso relayé au MATM et à la Justice
items.description: Le ministre d’État, ministre de l’Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité, Emile Zerbo, a présidé, ce lundi 5 octobre 2026 à l’Immeuble du Faso, à Ouagadougou, la traditionnelle montée des couleurs. La cérémonie qui se tient dans le cadre de la deuxième phase de l’édition 2026 des Journées d’engagement patriotique et de participation citoyenne (JEPPC), a été co-organisée avec le ministère de la Justice, en présence de son chef de département, Me Edasso Rodrigue Bayala. Sous le regard des acteurs du monde judiciaire et des personnels des deux départements ministériels, les agents du ministère de l’Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité et ceux du ministère de la Justice ont entonné en chœur l’hymne national en dioula, tandis que le drapeau burkinabè était hissé. La cérémonie a également servi de cadre à Emile Zerbo pour livrer le message du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, autour du thème de cette édition : « Produisons burkinabè, consommons burkinabè ! » . Le ministre Émile Zerbo a porté le message du Chef de l'État à ses collaborateurs Reprenant ce mot d’ordre, le ministre a appelé à aller plus loin dans l’engagement en faveur de la production et de la consommation locales. « Pour cette phase 2, voici le nouveau mot d'ordre : “Tous pour le Made in Burkina : Faisons de chaque achat un acte de souveraineté”. Car c'est de nos champs, de nos ateliers, de nos boutiques et de nos tables que se construit une nation debout, fière et souveraine », a-t-il martelé. Pour Emile Zerbo, la production, la transformation et la consommation constituent les trois maillons d’une même chaîne. « Si l’un de ces maillons cède, toute la chaîne se fragilise », a-t-il indiqué, estimant que « celui qui vous nourrit finit par vous dicter sa volonté ». Selon le ministre, trois principaux verrous entretiennent la dépendance du Burkina Faso. Il s'agit de la faiblesse de la production, de la transformation et de la consommation des produits locaux. Il a ainsi interpellé les différents acteurs de cette chaîne. Aux producteurs, il a réaffirmé la volonté de faire des paysans « des acteurs économiques puissants, organisés, bien outillés, justement rémunérés et pleinement conscients de leur rôle ». Emile Zerbo reprenant le message du Président du Faso, a salué le rôle des femmes productrices, transformatrices, commerçantes et tisseuses, notamment dans la production du soumbala, du dèguè, des farines infantiles, du beurre de karité et du Faso Dan Fani. Les agents des deux ministères mobilisés Les artisans, commerçants et industriels ont, eux aussi, été appelés à accompagner la dynamique. « Quant à nos transformateurs et transformatrices, faites grandir nos capacités de transformation, de l’atelier à la manufacture, et de la manufacture à l’usine, puis portez nos produits jusqu’au marché, sous le label “Made in Burkina” » , a-t-il déclaré. Dans son intervention, le ministre a par ailleurs dénoncé la fraude, la contrebande, les fausses déclarations, la spéculation, la rétention des stocks et le dénigrement des produits locaux. Il a notamment pointé les pratiques visant à contourner la préférence nationale dans les marchés publics. Pour lever ces obstacles, Emile Zerbo a préconisé le renforcement de la production à travers la mécanisation, les aménagements hydro-agricoles, l’accès aux intrants et le développement des coopératives villageoises. Il a également insisté sur la transformation, la normalisation, l’emballage, la labellisation et la protection du « Made in Burkina ». S’agissant de la consommation, il a souhaité que la préférence nationale devienne la règle dans la commande publique et les cantines de l’État. « Je demande aux Burkinabè de traduire leur patriotisme en actes simples au quotidien. Demandez l’origine des produits avant leur prix, choisissez les produits burkinabè lorsqu’un équivalent existe, servez au moins un repas entièrement burkinabè chaque jour, privilégiez les mets, boissons et tenues du pays lors des cérémonies et mettez les produits locaux en première ligne dans les rayons » , a-t-il invité. Vers un marché davantage intégré au sein de la Confédération des États du Sahel Au-delà du marché national, Emile Zerbo lisant le message du Président du Faso, a appelé au renforcement des échanges au sein de la Confédération des États du Sahel et à une plus grande intégration des marchés africains. « Avec nos frères de la Confédération des États du Sahel, ouvrons davantage nos marchés les uns aux autres : le lait de nos éleveurs, le riz de nos bas-fonds, le bétail de nos savanes et les tissus de nos métiers à tisser » , a-t-il indiqué. En guise de conclusion, le ministre de l’Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité a lancé un appel aux Burkinabè. « Au champ, produisons burkinabè ! À l’usine, transformons burkinabè ! Au marché, achetons burkinabè ! À table, consommons burkinabè ! » , a-t-il lancé. Sidziguin Irène Corinne SAWADOGO Minute.bf JEPPC, montée des couleurs, Made in Burkina, souveraineté, consommation locale, Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, Emile Zerbo, Minute.bf

items.title: Salomey Awiti-Baffoe’s lawyers welcome GH¢100,000 bail after earlier rejection
items.description: Lawyer for senior nursing officer Salomey Awiti-Baffoe says the GH¢100,000 bail granted to his client by the Adenta Circuit Court is a relief after an earlier bail application was rejected by the High Court. Lead counsel Enoch Anhwere Afoakwa said the legal team is grateful to the court for granting Ms Awiti-Baffoe bail and is working to satisfy the conditions to secure her release. “In fact, we are extremely happy and grateful to the court for granting Madam Salomey Awiti-Baffoe bail this morning,” he said. The court granted the accused bail in the sum of GH¢100,000 with two sureties, both of whom must be civil servants earning not less than GH¢3,000 per month. Mr Afoakwa said the legal team is taking steps to secure suitable sureties and complete the administrative processes required for her release. “We believe that the process will move faster so that liberty, as the court has ordered, will be restored,” he said. Ms Awiti-Baffoe is facing an alleged false news publication charge linked to the Ghana Jollof TikTok case. According to her lawyer, although she has been affected by her time in custody, the immediate priority is to secure her release and allow the legal process to continue. The case has been adjourned to February 18, 2027, when the prosecution is expected to proceed with the matter and serve the defence with the relevant disclosure documents.

items.title: US withdraws all bomber aircraft from UK airbase used during Iran war
items.description: The United States confirmed that it had withdrawn all B-1 bombers from the British airbase of RAF Fairford, reportedly due to “new threats”, with Britain’s government insisting on Monday that the site is safe. Police were called to the base in southwest England on Sept 27 after a local farmer reported a group of men with several vans engaged in “suspicious” activity. The scare prompted a counter-terrorism probe and forced evacuations at 85 homes near the airbase, which was used by the US to launch strikes on Iran. Investigators did not find any explosives in the vans, but “a quantity of petrol was recovered”, according to counter-terrorism police. A statement from a Pentagon official on Sunday said, “We can acknowledge now that all US bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have redeployed to their home stations in the United States.” The statement noted that “operational security precluded us from confirming the movement of our assets and forces in real-time”. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Monday expressed “confidence in the security of all of our bases”. US facilities “theoretically could be threatened at any moment, and that’s why there’s so much security built around them”, Rubio said, adding that Washington had worked with London on the investigation and “they couldn’t be more cooperative”. An unidentified US official told CNN that the bombers were moved after “an unspecified new threat”, with the source calling the latest threat a “real world incident”. It was unusual to move the bombers back to their home stations instead of deploying them to another base in the region, the official reportedly said. Two US officials told the New York Times that the bombers were moved after commanders received new threats about an alleged Iran-backed plot against the base. One American official said the new information was part of the same threat warnings that surfaced three weeks ago, but the situation became urgent in the past 24 hours, NYT reported. Asked whether the base was safe, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s official spokesman said: “Yes.” “We have tried and tested approaches to defend our bases around the country and throughout the world,” he told reporters. Heightened security Speculation about the motives behind the incident ranged from terror threat to fuel theft, as energy prices in the UK hit record highs this week. Burnham has said there were “strong indications that Iran played a part” in the incident, a charge rejected by Tehran . Six London-based Britons arrested in the September incident, including a UK-Iranian dual national , all men in their mid-20s, were released on bail , drawing rebuke from Washington. “I wouldn’t have done that,” US President Donald Trump told reporters, while Rubio alleged a “foreign actor” was involved. View this post on Instagram Iran’s embassy in London said it “categorically rejects and strongly condemns” speculation that Tehran was involved. Adding to the mystery, British media reported that officers were alerted to the incident by one of the initial suspects, but police have not commented on the reports. Security at the base had reportedly been heightened recently. Britain gave Washington permission in March to use Fairford for “specific defensive operations into Iran”, and US bombers and other planes have since been seen taking off and landing at the base. Fairford is the only airbase on Britain’s mainland used for this purpose. The incident came after a farmer living in the village of Whelford, near the airbase, called the police after seeing three vans blocking a road and a group of masked men fleeing the scene. Aerial footage of the vans showed they appeared to contain barrels, and at least one was marked with a fake logo and phone number, giving the false impression that it was owned by a legitimate diesel delivery firm.

items.title: Maroc : plus de 60.900 entreprises créées en sept mois
items.description: Le nombre d'entreprises créées au Maroc s'est établi à 60.908 unités au terme des sept premiers mois de 2026, selon l'Office marocain de la propriété industrielle et commerciale (OMPIC). Ces entreprises se répartissent sur les personnes morales (45.898 unités) et les personnes physiques (15.010 unités), précise l'OMPIC dans un communiqué. S'agissant des formes juridiques, la Société à Responsabilité Limitée à Associé Unique (SARL AU) demeure la structure la plus adoptée par les créateurs d'entreprises personnes morales, avec une part de 65% des immatriculations. Elle est suivie par la Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) qui représente 33,9%. Sur le plan territorial, la région de Casablanca-Settat se classe en tête en concentrant 39,3% des créations d’entreprises personnes morales, devançant les régions de Rabat-Salé-Kénitra (14,5%), Marrakech-Safi (12,3%) et Tanger-Tétouan-Al Hoceima (10,8%). À elles seules, ces quatre régions regroupent 76,9% des créations d'entreprises personnes morales au niveau national. Concernant les secteurs d'activités, les entreprises personnes morales nouvellement créées exercent principalement dans le commerce (27,22%), suivi du BTP (Bâtiment et travaux publics) et activités Immobilières (25,28%), des services divers (20,03%), du transport (7,63%) et de l'industrie (6,3%). Pour ce qui est des entreprises individuelles (personnes physiques), la région de Tanger-Tétouan-Al Hoceima arrive en première position avec 20,6% des immatriculations, suivie de Casablanca-Settat (13,2%) et de Rabat-Salé-Kénitra (10,7%). Par ailleurs, 77.883 noms commerciaux (certificats négatifs) ont été délivrés par l'OMPIC durant la période allant de janvier à juillet 2026. items.title: Trafic de drogue : les premières peines de mort prononcées en Algérie
items.description: L’Algérie a durci sensiblement sa législation anti-drogue. Alors que la décision d'ouvrir une prison de haute sécurité dans le désert de Tanezrouft pour les narcotrafiquants a été prise, les premières condamnations à mort à l'encontre de trafiquants de drogue ont été prononcées ce lundi 5 octobre. Saisie de 113 Kg de cocaïne : la justice prononce 9 condamnations à mort Le tribunal criminel d’Alger a condamné à la peine capitale 9 individus, dont 6 par contumace, dans une affaire de trafic de cocaïne et de psychotropes, en vertu des dispositions de la loi 25-03 du 1er juillet 2025 relative à la prévention de la consommation de stupéfiants et de substances psychotropes et à la lutte contre leur usage et leur trafic illicites. Selon un communiqué de la Cour d'Alger, l'affaire jugée porte sur le trafic d'une énorme quantité de drogues dures (113 kilogrammes de cocaïne) et de psychotropes (plus de 225 000 comprimés de prégabaline). Les mis en cause sont poursuivis pour les crimes d’“importation, transport, expédition et stockage en vue de la vente de drogues dures et de substances psychotropes, dans le cadre d'une organisation criminelle, dans le but de porter atteinte à la sécurité nationale et de troubler l'ordre et la sécurité publics”, ainsi que pour les délits de “contrebande, usurpation d'identité, immigration clandestine, séjour irrégulier et blanchiment d'argent.” L’accusé principal est un jeune de 22 ans L'affaire remonte à septembre 2025 lorsque la police a saisi à M’sila 113 kg de cocaïne et 225 097 comprimés de prégabaline. Selon le journal El Moudjahid , le réseau est constitué de 16 membres, dont un ressortissant guinéen. Neuf personnes ont été arrêtées et présentées devant la justice. Selon la même source, l'accusé principal est un jeune de 22 ans. La semaine passée, l’Assemblée populaire nationale (APN) a adopté un projet d’amendement du Code pénal rétablissant l’exécution de la peine de mort pour certains crimes graves, comme la provocation volontaire d’incendies et l’enlèvement d’enfants. L’Algérie observe un moratoire sur l’exécution de la peine capitale depuis 1993. L’article Trafic de drogue : les premières peines de mort prononcées en Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

Fortes pluies : le plan d’urgence régional déclenché à Dakar (Vidéo)
items.description: Le Premier ministre, Ahmadou Alhaminou M. Lô, a annoncé, lundi 5 octobre, le déclenchement du plan d’urgence régional à Dakar, ainsi que la mise en place d’un comité de veille, à la suite des fortes précipitations enregistrées au Sénégal. « Le plan d’urgence régional va être déclenché pour nous permettre d’être en veille permanente », a déclaré le chef du gouvernement à l’issue d’une réunion d’urgence consacrée à la situation. La rencontre, présidée par le Premier ministre, a réuni notamment les ministres de l’Intérieur, de l’Éducation, de la Famille de l'Action sociale et des Solidarités, le ministre de l'Assainissement, le ministre des Forces Armées, le ministre des Infrastructures, le ministre des Transports, les représentants des ministères de la Santé et des Finances, afin de faire le point, sur les conséquences des intempéries et de coordonner la réponse des pouvoirs publics. Ahmadou Alhaminou Lô a donné des instructions pour renforcer la surveillance et anticiper une éventuelle aggravation de la situation. Cette vigilance est d’autant plus nécessaire que de « fortes probabilités » de pluies sont annoncées entre mardi et mercredi. « Il s’agit de passer en revue la situation », a expliqué le Premier ministre, qui assure que le gouvernement demeure particulièrement attentif à l’évolution des conditions météorologiques et à leurs conséquences sur les populations. Dans le volet humanitaire, la ministre de la Famille et des Solidarités a été instruite d’apporter, « sans tarder », secours et assistance aux sinistrés ainsi qu’aux populations affectées ou en situation de besoin. Au terme de la réunion, le Premier ministre a, au nom du président de la République, présenté ses condoléances et exprimé sa compassion aux familles touchées par les conséquences de ces fortes précipitations. Le déclenchement du dispositif régional vise ainsi à maintenir une veille permanente, à anticiper de nouvelles précipitations et à assurer une réponse coordonnée des services de l’État face aux éventuels nouveaux impacts. items.title: Bangladeshi Police Round Up Opposition Supporters
items.description: Click to expand Image Police officers in Dhaka, Bangladesh, July 9, 2024. © 2024 Sipa via AP Images The mass arrest of attendees at a small left-wing party’s meeting in Dhaka on September 26 is the latest incident in the Bangladesh authorities’ ongoing assault on civil and political rights. Police took around 290 supporters of the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal into custody after members of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party’s youth wing – the Jubo Dal-- claimed the gathering was a “secret” meeting of the former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League, which is banned. A court remanded 27 of those arrested to custody, because it was alleged they had chanted the slogan “Joy Bangla” (Victory to Bengal), a slogan associated with the Awami League. The Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal was part of a 14-party alliance, led by the Awami League, that governed Bangladesh from 2009 until 2024, when it was toppled by student led protests in which hundreds were killed by security forces. The current ruling party, the Bangladesh National Party, faced severe repression under the Awami League government. Since being elected in February, it has targeted its own perceived opponents with arbitrary detention and hundreds of Awami League members are currently in jail, mostly without charge. Police have repeatedly raided alleged gatherings of Awami League supporters. On September 26, the same day as the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal meeting, police in Barisal detained 12 Awami League activists for allegedly holding a "secret" meeting to “plan sabotage”; two days later, 15 were arrested in Dhaka under the Anti-Terrorism Act on similar allegations. In both cases those detained said they had gathered to mark Sheikh Hasina’s birthday. During Sheikh Hasina’s authoritarian rule, there were widespread and grave rights violations—including extra-judicial killings, enforced disappearances, torture and the arbitrary detention of political opponents. The Bangladesh Nationalist Party came to power promising to restore human rights and the rule of law. Instead, the new government has arbitrarily detained perceived opponents and rolled back human rights safeguards the interim government proposed. International human rights law guarantees freedoms of expression and association for all. Past violations of those rights committed when the Awami League was in power cannot justify the Bangladesh Nationalist Party’s current violations of the same rights. Bangladeshi history is rife with examples of where such repression can lead.

items.title: Domestic tourism and its impact on the local economy
items.description: Tourism is the activity of people moving from their usual places of residence to another destination, either within their own country or another country, for purposes such as leisure, recreation, business, education, culture, and more. Domestic tourism refers to travel and movement within the geographical boundaries of one’s own country, away from one’s usual place of residence, for a temporary period. It is a part of the tourism industry that encourages citizens to explore and appreciate the natural, historical, cultural, and recreational attractions available in their own country. The purpose of the trip may include leisure, education, cultural activities, visiting friends, and many more. For example, if a person travels to Kumasi, the Volta Region, or Cape Coast, they are practising domestic tourism. The growth of domestic tourism is important for local government because local governments are responsible for managing and developing the communities where many tourist attractions are located. When people travel within the country, they spend money on accommodation, food, transportation, attractions, entertainment, and locally produced goods. This economic activity benefits businesses and communities while also providing opportunities for local governments to generate revenue through permits, licenses, fees, tolls, and other locally generated funds. The revenue generated can support the provision and improvement of local services and infrastructure. Therefore, domestic tourism can contribute to local economic development, while local government plays a role in creating an environment that supports tourism through infrastructure, sanitation, security, regulation, and the protection of local attractions. Domestic Tourism plays an important role in developing the tourism industry. It creates opportunities for local businesses, promotes cultural understanding, generates employment, and encourages people to appreciate the attractions and heritage found within their own country. However, domestic tourism can also create environmental and social challenges when it is not properly managed. One of the major impacts of domestic tourism on local government is increased economic activity. When people travel to tourist destinations within their country, they spend money on accommodation, food, transportation, entertainment, entrance fees, and locally produced goods. This increased spending supports businesses operating within local communities. Local governments can also benefit from increased revenue through various taxes, levies, permits, licenses, and fees paid by tourism-related businesses. The additional revenue can provide local authorities with resources to support public services and community development projects. Domestic tourism contributes to employment within local communities. Tourism activities require workers such as tour guides, drivers, hotel and restaurant employees, vendors, artisans, cleaners, security personnel, and event organisers. As tourism demand increases, local businesses may employ more people. For local governments, increased employment can contribute to improved living standards and reduce unemployment within their communities. It can also increase the number of people participating in local economic activities and reduce dependence on government assistance. The growth of domestic tourism can encourage local governments to improve infrastructure in tourist destinations. Roads, transportation systems, public toilets, waste-management facilities, water supply, electricity, recreational facilities, and communication networks may need to be improved to accommodate visitors. Although infrastructure development can require significant government investment, the improvements can benefit both tourists and residents. Better roads, sanitation facilities, transportation, and public spaces can improve the overall quality of life within the community. Domestic tourism can contribute to national pride and identity. When citizens visit important historical and cultural sites, they gain a better understanding of their country’s history and achievements. For example, in Ghana, visiting places such as Cape Coast Castle, Elmina Castle, Kakum National Park, Mole National Park, and the Volta Region’s natural attractions can help citizens understand and appreciate the country’s historical, cultural, and natural heritage. This appreciation can encourage citizens to help protect and promote their country’s heritage. However, Domestic tourism is also closely connected to domestic marketing, as effective marketing encourages citizens to travel within the country and spend on local products and services. Domestic marketing can strengthen the local economy through the SEWF concept—See Ghana, Eat Ghana, Wear Ghana, Feel Ghana, and Experience Ghana. This is because See Ghana encourages citizens to visit attractions such as Cape Coast Castle, Kakum National Park, Mole National Park and Wli Waterfalls, thereby creating income for hotels, tour guides, transport operators, restaurants and local vendors. Eat Ghana also promotes local foods such as fufu, waakye, banku and kenkey, and this supports farmers, food vendors, restaurants and other food-related businesses. Wear Ghana encourages the use of locally made products such as kente from Bonwire, smocks from the Northern Region and batik fabrics, providing income and employment for weavers, designers and traders across the country. Feel Ghana promotes rich Ghanaian culture through festivals, music, traditions and local entertainment, while Experience Ghana encourages people to participate in activities such as visiting cultural sites, exploring national parks and experiencing traditional festivals. SEWF therefore helps keep money within the local economy by encouraging people to spend on Ghanaian products, services and experiences. For example, when visitors travel to Kakum National Park, they may pay for transportation, accommodation, food, tour guides and locally made crafts, and this creates income for several businesses within the surrounding communities. Similarly, festivals such as the Homowo Festival in Greater Accra and the Aboakyere Festival in Winneba attract visitors who spend money on food, accommodation, transportation, clothing and entertainment. This creates employment, supports small and medium-sized businesses and provides additional income for local communities. Therefore, See Ghana, Eat Ghana, Wear Ghana, Feel Ghana and Experience Ghana can contribute to local economic growth by encouraging domestic spending, supporting local enterprises and promoting Ghanaian products and services. According to the 2025 Ghana Tourism report, domestic tourism in Ghana was largely concentrated around major tourist destinations. The country’s ten most popular tourist sites recorded 1,377,588 visits, representing 77% of total domestic visitations. This demonstrates the strong attraction of Ghana’s historical, cultural, and natural tourism sites to domestic visitors. The Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park recorded the highest visitation, attracting 302,523 visitors and maintaining its position as the country’s leading tourist site. It was followed by Kakum National Park, which recorded 203,222 visits, while Bunso Arboretum ranked third with 149,319 visitors. Other highly visited destinations included Cape Coast Castle, with 141,523 visitors, and Manhyia Palace Museum, which recorded 120,328 visits. Kumasi Zoo, Accra Zoo, Elmina Castle, Shai Hills Resource Reserve, and Aburi Botanical Garden also featured among the top ten tourist sites. In conclusion, domestic tourism has significant impacts on local government and the communities they serve. It can generate revenue, create employment, support local businesses, improve infrastructure, promote cultural heritage, and encourage development in rural and less-developed areas. At the same time, increased tourism can strain public services, infrastructure, and the environment. Therefore, local governments need effective tourism planning and management to maximise the benefits while reducing the negative effects. When properly managed, domestic tourism can become an important tool for local economic development, community improvement, and sustainable development. – By Worklatsi John Edem Intern, Corporate Affairs Department Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA)
